title: God's Beef with His People
paragraphs: Okay, so this is the vision Isaiah, son of Amoz, had about Judah and Jerusalem. This all went down when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.

God's laying out his case, and he's calling on heaven and earth to be the jury. He's like, "Listen, I raised these kids, gave them everything, and they just straight up turned on me. Even an ox knows its owner, and a donkey knows who feeds it, but Israel? My own people? They're clueless. It's a total shame. These guys are God-dropouts, just weighed down by their own baggage of bad choices. A whole crew of villains, a gang of vandals. My people have ghosted me, their God, turned their backs on the Holy One of Israel, and just walked away without a second thought.

"Honestly, why do I even bother trying with you guys? You're so stubborn. It's like you're intentionally running into brick walls. Your whole being is fighting against you. From your feet to your head, nothing is right. You're covered in wounds, bruises, and nasty sores that are just left there—no one's cleaning them, no one's bandaging them up. Your country is a wreck, your cities are burned to the ground. Foreigners are taking over your land right in front of you, and it's just a pile of rubble left by barbarians. Daughter Zion is all alone, like a beat-up shack on a dead-end road, like a rundown shanty on the wrong side of town, or a sinking ship everyone's bailed on. Honestly, if God-of-the-Angel-Armies hadn’t left a few of us, we'd be totally wiped out like Sodom, completely doomed like Gomorrah.
"So listen up, you leaders who are basically schooled by Sodom. Pay attention to God's revelation, you people who are learning from Gomorrah.

"For real, why all these sacrifices?" God is asking. "You think I'm not sick of all the burnt offerings, the rams, and the fat calves? You think I want all this blood from bulls, lambs, and goats? When you show up in my house, who even told you to act like this, running all over the place, doing whatever? It's just chaos in the place where you're supposed to worship.

"Just stop with the fake worship. I can't stand your pointless religious games. All your monthly meetings, weekly Sabbaths, special get-togethers—meetings, meetings, and more meetings—I can't take it anymore! Meetings for this, meetings for that. I hate them! You've completely worn me out! I'm so over your religion, religion, religion, especially when you just keep on sinning. Next time you put on a big prayer show, I'm gonna be looking the other way. It doesn't matter how long or loud you pray, I'm not listening. And you know why? Because you've been tearing people apart, and your hands are covered in blood. Go home and wash up. Get your act together. Clean up your lives from all the evil stuff so I don't have to see it anymore. Say no to what's wrong. Learn to do good. Fight for justice. Help out people who are struggling. Stand up for the homeless. Go to bat for those who can't defend themselves.

"Come on. Sit down. Let's talk this through." This is God's message: "If your sins are as red as blood, they'll be as white as snow. If they're crimson red, they'll be like wool. If you're willing to listen and obey, you'll live like kings. But if you're stubborn and refuse, you'll die like dogs." God said it.

Can you even believe this? The city that was once so pure has become a total sellout! It used to be all about justice, everyone was a good neighbor, and now they're all at each other's throats. Your money is fake. Your wine is watered down. Your leaders are traitors who hang out with criminals. They'll do anything for money and take whatever they can get. They never stand up for the homeless or defend those who need help.

So, this is the official decree from the Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the Strong One of Israel: "That's it! I'm gonna get these oppressors off my back. I'm getting back at my enemies. I'm about to lay down the law, get all the junk out of your life, and clean you up. I'm going to set up honest judges and wise counselors for you, just like it was in the good old days. Then you'll be called 'The City That Does Right' and 'The Real-Deal City.'" God's right ways will make Zion right again. His right actions will bring back his lost kids. But it's game over for the rebels and God-traitors, a dead end for anyone who walks out on God. "All your messing around in those sacred tree groves is gonna make you look so foolish, and all that fooling around in those god and goddess gardens you thought was so cool. You'll end up like an oak tree losing all its leaves, like a garden with no water, all withered and brown. The 'Strong Man' will turn out to be nothing but dead twigs, and his 'great work' will be the spark that starts a fire that burns it all down to nothing but smoke."

title: God's Mountain is the GOAT, No More War!
paragraphs: Here’s the vision Isaiah had about Judah and Jerusalem: Okay, so check it. A day is coming when the mountain with God's house on it will be THE mountain, like, towering over all the others. People from every country will be streaming towards it. They'll be like, 'Yo, let's go up to God's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God. He'll teach us his ways so we can live how we're supposed to.' The real message is gonna come from Zion; God's message is gonna broadcast from Jerusalem. He'll sort out all the drama between countries and make things fair for everyone. They'll trade their swords for garden tools and their spears for farming equipment. No more country-on-country beef; they won't even train for war anymore. So let's go, fam of Jacob, let's live in God's light.

God, you've bounced on your people, the family of Jacob, and it's because they're into all this fake religion, sketchy Philistine magic, and weird pagan stuff. Their world is all about getting rich, having endless stuff, and all the latest gadgets. And the idols—so many idols of all shapes and sizes. These people literally make their own gods and then bow down to them. It's a total mess, they're face-down in the mud. Just leave them be, God. They're not even worth forgiving.
Run for the hills, hide in a cave from God's terrifying and awesome presence.

All the arrogant people are about to get humbled, and all the cocky attitudes will be shut down. On that day, it's gonna be all about God. The Day of the Lord of Angel Armies is coming for anyone with a big ego, anyone who thinks they're all that. He's coming for the huge, towering sequoia trees and the massive chestnut trees. He's coming for the biggest mountains like Kilimanjaro and Annapurna, and the epic ranges like the Alps and Andes. He's coming for every crazy-tall skyscraper and all the proud monuments. He's coming for the fancy cruise ships and the slick sailing yachts. All those inflated egos are gonna get popped, and the proud people will be brought back down to reality. On that day, God alone will be the center of attention.
And all those fake gods they made out of sticks and stones? They're gonna be gone for good.

Scramble into the caves in the cliffs, dive into any hole you can find. You gotta hide from the terror of God, from his blinding glory, when he finally stands up and shows his true, terrifying power on earth.

On that day, people will take all their gold and silver idols—the ones they made and worshipped—and just toss them into a ditch. Then they'll run for the caves and hideouts in the cliffs to escape from the terror of God and his awesome presence, when he rises to shake the earth.
Seriously, stop idolizing mere humans. They're so full of themselves and just a bunch of hot air. Can't you see there's nothing to them?

title: God Calls Out the Fakes
paragraphs: Okay, so check it. The Master, God of the Angel Armies, is about to pull the plug on Jerusalem and Judah. We're talking total resource drain, starting with the basics like bread and water. He's taking away all the people who keep things running: the cops, the judges, the pastors, the teachers, the military leaders, the doctors, the nurses, and even the handymen. He's basically like, 'I'm gonna put a bunch of kids in charge. Literal middle schoolers will be running the show.' And it's gonna be chaos. People will be turning on each other, backstabbing left and right. Neighbors fighting neighbors, the young disrespecting the old, and the nobodies trying to take down the popular kids. It'll get so bad that one brother will grab another and be like, 'Dude, you look like you have your life together. You gotta do something and get us out of this mess.' But the other guy will just be like, 'Me? Nah, man. I'm clueless. Don't put me in charge of anything.'

Jerusalem is on its last legs, for real. Judah is about to get knocked out. Everything they say and do is basically a slap in the face to God. They're not even trying to hide their messed-up lives; they're flaunting their sins like they're proud of it, just like the people of Sodom. Doom to them. They made their bed, and now they gotta lie in it.

But for the good people, tell them it's all good. Their righteous living is gonna pay off, big time. But for the wicked? It's over for them. Disaster is coming. Everything they did to others is about to be done right back to them.

My people are being terrorized by a bunch of skinny kids. Silly girls are pushing them around. Seriously, my people! Your leaders are leading you down a dead-end street. They're sending you on a wild-goose chase that goes nowhere.

God is stepping into the courtroom. He's taking His seat on the judge's bench to judge His own people. God's calling for order and putting the leaders on trial. He's like, 'You've wrecked this country. Your houses are full of stuff you stole from the poor. What's up with that? You're stomping all over my people and grinding the faces of the poor into the dirt?' That's a direct quote from the Master, God of the Angel Armies.

God says, 'The women of Zion are so stuck-up. They prance around in their high heels, trying to catch every guy's eye on the street, swinging their hips and tossing their hair. They're all flashy and tacky with their cheap jewelry.' But the Master is gonna make all those Zion women go bald. Like, scabby, bald-headed women. The Master is gonna do it.

The time is coming when the Master will strip them of all their fancy accessories—the dangly earrings, anklets, and bracelets, the combs, mirrors, and silk scarves, the diamond pins and pearl necklaces, the rings on their fingers and toes, the trendy hats, the expensive perfumes and whatever else they use to feel attractive, the designer gowns and capes, all the finest clothes in the world.

Instead of smelling like seductive perfume, these women are going to stink like rotting cabbage. Instead of wearing beautiful gowns, they'll be in rags. Instead of their perfect hairstyles, they'll have scruffy, bald heads. Instead of beauty marks, they'll have scabs and scars.

Your best soldiers will be killed in battle, your warriors left dead on the field. The gates of Zion will be crowded with people crying over their dead. The whole city will be hunched over from the weight of its loss, brought to its knees by sorrow.

title: From Desperate Times to a Divine Glow-Up
paragraphs: Picture this: a time's coming when seven women will be all over one guy, like, 'Look, we've got our own food and clothes, we're independent. Just give us a baby. We need a reason to live, you know?'

But then God’s special Branch will shoot up, all green and awesome. The land will be so fruitful, and the survivors in Israel will finally have something to brag about. They'll be walking tall, for real. All the people left in Zion, even the ones who felt like outcasts in Jerusalem, will be called 'holy'—because they're alive, and that's what matters. God’s gonna wash the ladies of Zion clean, scrubbing away all the violence and nastiness from the city. He's gonna clean house with a fiery judgment, like a total reset.

And then, God will bring back that legendary pillar of cloud for the daytime and the pillar of fire for the night. He'll put his glorious, super-protective presence over Mount Zion and everyone there—like a giant umbrella from the scorching sun and a cozy shelter from the pouring rain.

title: God's Vineyard Totally Flops
paragraphs: Let me sing a love song for my friend, about his vineyard. My guy had this awesome vineyard on a perfect hill. He worked the ground, cleared the rocks, and planted the best vines you could find. He even built a watchtower and a winepress, super proud of it. He was expecting a great harvest of grapes, but after all that work, he just got a bunch of nasty, sour ones.

"Aight, listen up, people of Jerusalem and Judah. Tell me what you think is up with me and my vineyard. Is there anything else I could've possibly done for it? I did everything. So why, when I was hoping for some sweet grapes, did I get this bitter garbage?"

"So for real, let me tell you what I'm about to do to my vineyard. I'm tearing down the fence and letting it get wrecked. I'm gonna bust down the wall and let everything trample all over it. I'll just let it turn into a field of weeds, no one to take care of it. Thistles and thorns are gonna take over. I'll even tell the clouds, 'Don't you dare rain on that place, ever!'"

So, you get it? The vineyard of God, the Commander of Angel Armies, is Israel. The people of Judah are the garden he was so proud of. He was looking for justice, but instead, he saw them turning on each other. He wanted to see righteousness, but all he heard were the cries of people who were getting hurt.

Man, you guys are in deep trouble—you who buy up all the houses and snatch up all the land for yourselves. You kick out the original owners, put up 'No Trespassing' signs, and take over everything, leaving people with no place to live. I heard the God of Angel Armies say this: "All those huge houses? They're gonna be empty. Those fancy mansions will be ghost towns. A ten-acre vineyard will barely make a pint of wine, and a huge bag of seed will only grow a tiny bit of grain."

You're so done for—you who start drinking first thing in the morning and stay up all night getting wasted. You throw these huge parties with harps, flutes, and tons of wine, but you couldn't care less about what God is doing. You totally ignore his work. That's why my people are gonna get dragged off into exile—because they have no clue what's up. Their so-called 'important' people will starve, and everyone else will be dying of thirst. The underworld, Sheol, is super hungry, ready to swallow people whole. Big shots and nobodies, they're all going down, not to mention all the drunks. The poor will be on the same level as the rich, and all the arrogant boasters will be deflated like a popped balloon. But God, the Commander of Angel Armies, will be lifted up because he does what's right. The Holy God will show everyone what 'holy' really means by being righteous. And lambs will just chill and graze like they own the place, and little goats will hang out in the ruins.

You're in for it, you who use lies to push evil stuff and haul sin around by the truckload. The ones who say, "What's God waiting for? Tell him to hurry up so we can see what he's got. Whatever the Holy One of Israel is planning, we wanna see it."
You're in for it, you who call evil good and good evil, who switch out darkness for light and light for darkness, who say bitter is sweet and sweet is bitter!

You're in for it, you who think you're so smart and have such a high opinion of yourselves! The only thing you're good at is drinking. You're like champion drinkers who win trophies for it, and then you take bribes from guilty people while screwing over the innocent.

But you won't get away with it. Just like fire burns up straw and dry grass disappears in smoke, your very souls will rot, and everything you've built will turn to dust. Why? Because you rejected the word of the God of Angel Armies and wanted nothing to do with the Holy One of Israel.

That's why God got so mad at his people. He reached out and smacked them down. The mountains shook, and their dead bodies were just piled up in the streets. But even after all that, he was still furious, his fist still raised, ready to strike again. He's raising a flag to signal a nation far away, whistling for people from the ends of the earth. And look, here they come, running like crazy! No one is tired, no one trips, no one's even sleepy. Their shirts are tucked in, pants are buckled, and every boot is polished and tied. Their arrows are sharp, their bows are ready. Their horses' hooves are like iron, and their chariot wheels are greased. They roar like a bunch of lions, like young lions roaring with all their might. They growl and grab their prey, dragging it away where no one can save it. On that day, the roar will be like the roar of the ocean. If you look at the land, all you'll see is darkness and trouble. Every single light in the sky will be blacked out by clouds.

title: My INSANE Vision of God in Heaven (ft. 6-Winged Angels)
paragraphs: So, the year King Uzziah died, I had this amazing vision. I saw the Lord, and He was sitting on this massive throne, like, way up high. His robe was so huge it filled the entire Temple. These amazing angels called seraphs were flying above Him. Each one had six wings. They used two to cover their faces, two to cover their feet, and the other two to fly around. And they were all shouting to each other, 'Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Heaven's Armies! The whole earth is filled with His glory!' The sound of their voices was so powerful it shook the entire Temple, and the whole place filled up with smoke. It was wild. I was like, 'I'm so done for! It's over for me.' Because I'm a guy who says a lot of messed-up stuff, and I live with people who are just like me. And I've just seen the King, the LORD of Heaven's Armies, with my own eyes! Then one of the seraphs flew over to me. He was holding this glowing hot coal that he'd grabbed from the altar with some tongs. He touched my mouth with it and said, 'Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is gone. Your sin is forgiven.' And then I heard the Lord's voice say, 'Who should I send? Who will go for us?' And I was like, 'I’ll go. Send me!'

He said, 'Go and tell this people: 'Listen hard, but you aren’t going to get it; look hard, but you won’t catch on.' Make these people blockheads, with fingers in their ears and blindfolds on their eyes, so they won’t see a thing, won’t hear a word, so they won’t have a clue about what’s going on and, yes, so they won’t turn around and be made whole.'

I was shaken and asked, 'And Master, how long is this gonna go on?' He said, 'Until the cities are totally empty, not a single person left in them—houses empty, countryside empty. Until I, God, get rid of everyone, sending them away, and the land is completely deserted. And even if a few people are left, like a tenth of them, the destruction will just start all over again. The country will look like a forest where every single tree has been chopped down—just a huge field of stumps. But there’s a holy seed in those stumps.'

title: God's WILD Sign & A King Who Won't Listen
paragraphs: So, get this: while Ahaz was king of Judah, two other kings, Rezin of Aram and Pekah of Israel, tried to attack Jerusalem, but their plan totally failed. When King Ahaz and his people heard that Aram had teamed up with Israel, they were seriously shaken. Like, shaking like leaves in the wind.

Then God told the prophet Isaiah, “Go meet Ahaz. Take your son Shear-jashub with you. You'll find him at the end of the aqueduct by the public laundry road. Tell him, ‘Listen, you need to chill. Don’t be scared. And don’t panic over these two burnt-out kings, Rezin and Pekah. They talk a big game, but they’ve got nothing. Aram and Israel have plotted to mess you up, saying, ‘Let’s go destroy Judah, take it for ourselves, and make some random dude king.’

But God, the ultimate boss, says, “It’s not gonna happen. Nothing will come of it. Because Aram’s capital is just Damascus, and its king is just a man, Rezin. As for Israel, in 65 years it’ll be a total ruin, nothing left. Its capital is Samaria, and its king is just some guy. If you don’t have faith, you literally have nothing to stand on.”
God hit up Ahaz again, saying, “Ask for a sign from your God. Ask for anything. Go big. Ask for the moon!”
But Ahaz was like, “Nah, I’m good. I’d never test God like that.”

So Isaiah told him, “Okay, listen up, house of David. It’s bad enough you’re annoying everyone with your fake piety, but now you’re making God tired. So the Lord himself is gonna give you a sign anyway. Watch this: a young woman who’s a virgin will get pregnant. She’ll have a son and name him Immanuel, which means ‘God-With-Us.’ By the time he’s old enough to know right from wrong, the threat of war will be long gone. So relax, those two kings you’re so worried about will be history. But here’s the deal: God is about to bring a disaster on you, your people, and your government that’s worse than anything since the kingdom split up. The king of Assyria is coming!”
That’s when God will whistle for flies from Egypt and bees from Assyria. They’ll swarm every single part of the country. You won’t be able to escape them.

And that’s when the Lord will use a razor he rented from across the river—the king of Assyria himself—and shave your heads and your bodies, leaving you totally shamed and exposed. He’ll even shave off your beards.

It’ll be a time when survivors will feel lucky just to have a cow and a couple of sheep. At least they’ll have milk! Whoever is left in the land will have to live on simple stuff like curds and honey.

But it gets worse. This country that used to be full of amazing vineyards will turn into a giant patch of weeds. Weeds and thorns everywhere! It’ll only be good for hunting. Cows and sheep will have to find food in the weeds, and all those beautiful gardens and fields will be completely gone.

title: God's Plan is Lowkey Scary Good
paragraphs: So God was like, 'Yo, grab a huge poster board and write this down in permanent marker: 'This is for Maher-shalal-hash-baz,' which basically means 'Quick to Plunder, Swift to Spoil.'
I got a couple of legit guys, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah, to be official witnesses. Then I went home to my wife, who's also a prophet, and she got pregnant and had a baby boy.
God said, 'Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz. Before that kid can even say 'Dada' or 'Mama,' the king of Assyria is gonna roll in and take all the expensive stuff from Damascus and Samaria.'

Then God hit me up again and said: 'Since these people dissed the chill vibes of the Shiloah stream and are all hyped about Rezin and Remaliah's son, I'm about to bring the heat. I'm sending the crazy floodwaters of the Euphrates—that's the king of Assyria and his whole crew—like a river totally overflowing. It's gonna flood Judah, sweep away everything, with water up to your necks. It's gonna be like a massive, raging river, Immanuel, spreading all over your country.'

But for real, all you haters, you better get ready to be stressed. Listen up, everyone, no matter where you are. Brace yourselves, 'cause it's about to get bad. Yeah, for real, brace yourselves. You can make all the plans you want, but it's all gonna be for nothing. All your talk is just noise, empty words. Because at the end of the day, the final say belongs to Immanuel—which means God is with us.

God got super serious with me, like He grabbed me and was like, 'Don't even think about going along with these people.' He said: 'Don't be like these people, always paranoid that someone's plotting against them. Don't be scared of what they're scared of. Don't stress about their problems. If you're gonna stress about anything, stress about The Holy One. Fear God-of-the-Angel-Armies. The Holy One can be your safe space or a huge rock that trips you up, a boulder in the way for both houses of Israel, like a barbed-wire fence for the people of Jerusalem. A lot of them are gonna crash into that Rock and break their bones, get tangled in that barbed wire and be stuck.'

'So, hold on to this message, keep the teaching safe for my followers, while I wait for God, even though He's hiding right now. I'm gonna wait and hope for Him. I'm standing my ground and hoping, me and the kids God gave me. We're like warning signs and signs of hope for Israel, from God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who lives on Mount Zion.'

When people tell you, 'Go ask a fortune-teller. Talk to a psychic. Why not hit up the spirit world and talk to the dead?' You tell them, 'Nah, we're gonna stick to the Scriptures.' People who try that other stuff get absolutely nowhere—it's a total dead end! They get frustrated and desperate and try all sorts of things. When nothing works, they get mad and start cursing this god and that god, looking everywhere for answers—up, down, all around—and find nothing. Just a blank wall, an empty void. They just end up lost in the dark.

title: From Darkness to a GOATED King
paragraphs: But for real, for those who were in deep trouble, the darkness is over. A while back, God let the lands of Zebulun and Naphtali get dissed, but a time is coming when he’s gonna make that whole area glorious—the road by the sea, the land past the Jordan river, and Galilee where all the nations mix.

The people who were stumbling around in the dark? They’ve seen a massive light. For those living in a land of deep shadows—Light! Sunbursts of it! You made the nation huge again, and cranked up its joy. Oh, they’re so hyped in your presence! It’s a full-on festival vibe! Like the joy of a massive party, sharing awesome gifts and warm hellos. The abuse from oppressors and the cruelty of tyrants—all their whips and clubs and curses—it's all gone, finished. It was a rescue as surprising and sudden as Gideon’s legendary victory over Midian. The boots of all those invading soldiers, and their uniforms soaked in innocent blood, will be piled up and set on fire—a blaze that will burn for days! Because a child has been born—for us! The gift of a son—for us! He’s gonna take over running the world. His names are gonna be insane: Amazing Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace. His government will just keep growing, and the peace he brings will have no end. He’ll rule from the historic throne of David over that promised kingdom. He’ll make that kingdom solid and keep it going with fairness and justice, starting right now and lasting forever. The passion of the God of Angel Armies will make all this happen.

The Master sent a message to Jacob’s crew. It landed right on Israel’s doorstep. Everyone heard the message, from Ephraim to the people in Samaria. But they were a proud and arrogant bunch. They just brushed off the message, like, “Things aren’t that bad. We can handle whatever. If our buildings get knocked down, we’ll just rebuild them bigger and better. If our forests get chopped down, we’ll replant them with even nicer trees.”

So God basically set up their enemies against them, stirring them up to attack: Arameans from the east, Philistines from the west. They totally wrecked Israel. But even after all that, God was still angry, his fist still raised, ready to strike again.

But the people didn't even think about the one who was hitting them; they didn't look for the God of Angel Armies. So God chopped off Israel’s head and tail, the fancy palm branch and the lowly reed, all in one day. The “head” was the important elders, and the “tail” was the prophets who told lies. The ones who were supposed to lead the people led them down dead-end streets, and the ones who followed them ended up totally lost and confused. That’s why the Master wasn't feeling the young men anymore, and had no sympathy for their orphans and widows. Every single one of them was godless and evil, just talking trash and nonsense. And even after all that, he was still angry, his fist still raised, ready to hit them again.

Their evil lives spread like a wildfire out of control, the kind that just burns up everything in its way—trees, bushes, weeds, grass—and fills the sky with smoke. The God of Angel Armies fought fire with fire, setting the whole country ablaze. He turned the people into fires that consumed each other in their selfish desires—their appetites were bottomless, just stuffing themselves with people and things left and right. But they were still starving. Not even their own kids were safe from their greedy hunger. Manasseh went after Ephraim, and Ephraim went after Manasseh, and then the two of them ganged up on Judah. And even after that, he was still angry, his fist still raised, ready to hit them again.

title: God's Unexpected Flex on a Cocky Empire
paragraphs: Doom to you guys who make messed-up laws, the kind that totally screw people over. Laws that make life a nightmare for the poor, that steal their last bit of dignity. You're out here taking advantage of widows and homeless kids? Seriously? What are you gonna say when it's Judgement Day and everything hits the fan? Who's gonna have your back then? You think your money can save you? Nah. You'll be a sad sight, either locked up with the other prisoners or just another body in a pile on the street. And even after all that, God's still ticked off, ready to throw down again.

"Doom to Assyria, my weapon of anger right now. My anger is the club you're swinging. I'm sending you after a nation that's totally forgotten me, the people I'm so mad at. I'm telling you to go in, take everything they have, and just wreck the place. But Assyria? He's got his own plans. He's thinking bigger. He wants to completely wipe out as many nations as possible. He's out here bragging, 'Aren't my commanders basically kings? Don't they do whatever they want? I wrecked Calno and Carchemish. I took down Hamath and Arpad. I leveled Samaria just like I did with Damascus. I've taken out kingdoms with way more impressive gods than anything in Jerusalem and Samaria. So, for real, what's stopping me from doing the exact same thing to Jerusalem and all its little idols?'”

But when the Master is done with Mount Zion and Jerusalem, he's gonna be like, “Alright, Assyria, your turn.” I'm gonna humble that arrogant king of Assyria, with his cocky attitude and the way he walks around saying,

“‘I did all this myself. I'm a genius. I redrew the maps of countries. I walked in and took whatever I wanted. I was like a beast, knocking kings off their thrones. I just reached out and snatched all their treasure, easy as grabbing eggs from a bird's nest. I gathered up the whole world like it was nothing, and nobody even made a peep or tried to stop me.’”

For real though, does an ax get credit for the chopping? Does a saw act like it's more important than the person using it? That's like a shovel thinking it's doing the digging, not the person holding it! Or a hammer thinking it's using the carpenter to hit nails! Because of this, the Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, is gonna send a sickness to take down Assyria's tough-guy fighters. Under God's glorious light, a fire is gonna start. Israel's Light will become a huge blaze, the Holy One will be a firestorm, and in one day, it's gonna burn every last one of those Assyrian thorns to ash. God's gonna destroy their amazing forests and gardens. The whole of Assyria, body and soul, will just waste away like someone with a terminal illness. A little kid could count the trees they have left on two hands.

And on that day, the leftovers of Israel, the survivors of Jacob's crew, will finally stop leaning on abusive Assyria. They'll lean on God, the Holy One—for real this time. The small group that's left, the remnant of Jacob, will come back to the Strong God. Your people, Israel, were once as many as the grains of sand on the beach, but only a few will make it back. Destruction is coming, and it's overflowing with justice. Because the Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, is gonna finish what he started, right here and all over the world.

So the Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, says: “My people living in Zion, don't freak out when the Assyrians beat you with clubs and threaten you like the Egyptians did way back. In just a little bit, my anger at you will be over, and then I'll turn my destructive anger on them. I, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, will come after them with a whip and finish them off for good—just like Gideon wrecked Midian at the rock of Oreb, and like Moses flipped the script on Egypt. On that day, Assyria's weight will be lifted off your back, and the chains of slavery will be broken from your neck.”

Assyria is on the move: they're coming up from Rimmon, heading to Aiath, through Migron, and setting up a base at Micmash. They've crossed the pass and are camping at Geba for the night. The town of Ramah is shaking. Gibeah of Saul has already bounced. Scream for help, Gallim! Listen up, Laishah! Do something, Anathoth! Madmenah is running for the hills. The people of Gebim are in full-on panic mode. The enemy is almost at Nob—so close! You can see him from the city, shaking his fist at the mountain of dear daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.

But watch this: The Master, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, is about to swing his ax and chop off the branches. He's gonna cut down the giant trees and flatten the whole marching forest. His ax is gonna turn that forest into toothpicks, that whole Lebanon-level army will be nothing but kindling.

title: The World's Gonna Be GOATED
paragraphs: So, check it: A fresh, new shoot is gonna grow from the old stump of Jesse's family tree, like a new branch budding out. God's life-giving Spirit will be all over this guy, giving him major wisdom and understanding. This Spirit will show him the way, make him strong, and fill him with knowledge and a deep respect for God. And that respect for God? That's what he'll be all about. He won't be judging people based on how they look or what he's heard. Nah, he'll make things right for the poor and needy, serving up some real justice. When he speaks, everyone will be hanging on his every word, totally captivated. A single word from him will be enough to take down the bad guys. Every day, he'll be up and at it, ready to work, building a world that's fair and true.

Get this: wolves and lambs will be chilling together, and leopards will be napping with baby goats. Calves and lions will be eating from the same bowl, and a little kid will be their babysitter. Cows and bears will be grazing in the same field, their babies growing up together. And lions will be eating hay like cows! It's gonna be so peaceful that a baby could crawl over a snake's nest, and a toddler could stick their hand in a viper's den without getting hurt. On God's holy mountain, nobody and nothing will be hurting or killing each other. The whole world will be filled with the knowledge of the living God, like a huge ocean of understanding.
On that day, this descendant of Jesse will be like a huge banner, raised up for everyone to see. People from all over the world will flock to him, and his home base will be absolutely glorious.

And on that day, the Lord will, for the second time, reach out and bring back the rest of his scattered people. He'll gather them from all over the place—from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Ethiopia, Elam, Babylonia, Hamath, and even from faraway islands.

He'll raise this banner high for all the nations to see, and he'll bring back all the exiled people of Israel. He'll gather all the scattered people of Judah from every corner of the earth. The jealousy between Ephraim and Judah will be gone, and the hostility will disappear. Ephraim won't be jealous of Judah anymore, and Judah won't be hostile to Ephraim. They'll be like brothers, united. They'll team up and take down their enemies, the Philistines in the west and the people in the east. They'll even conquer Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will have to obey them. God will dry up the Red Sea in Egypt again, making it easy to cross. He'll send a scorching wind on the great Euphrates River, splitting it into seven small streams so that people can cross without even getting their feet wet. In the end, there will be a highway from Assyria for the rest of God's people, just like there was for Israel when they came out of Egypt.

title: God's Epic Takedown of Babylon
paragraphs: This is the message about Babylon that Isaiah, son of Amoz, saw.

"Put a flag up on a bare hill. Shout out, get their attention. Wave them over, get them in formation, and send them straight to the heart of the powerful city. I've personally gathered my special crew, my elite squad. They're super hyped and ready to unleash my anger."

The sound of a massive, rowdy crowd rumbles from the mountains. It's the thunder of kingdoms getting riled up, nations gathering for a fight. The LORD of Heaven's Armies is getting his soldiers ready for battle. They're coming from super far away, pouring in from all over the world. It's God making his move with his weapons of fury, about to wreck the whole country.

Cry out! The LORD's day of judgment is coming, and it's gonna hit like an avalanche from the Almighty God. Everyone's gonna be frozen in fear, totally freaking out and losing it. They'll be doubled over in pain, like a woman in labor. It's gonna be wild—everyone they see will look like something from a horror movie.

"Alright, check it. The LORD's judgment day is on its way. It's gonna be brutal, a day of pure rage and anger. A day to totally trash the earth and get rid of all the sinners. The stars, even the coolest constellations, will just be black holes in the sky. The sun will rise as a black circle, and the moon will be a total blank. I'm gonna end all the evil in the world, shut down all the wicked stuff people do. I'm gonna silence all the arrogant people—not another word from them—and take down all the proud tyrants, leaving them face down in the dirt. Humans are gonna become super rare, rarer than pure gold. And yeah, I'm even gonna make the sky tremble and the earth shake to its core because of the anger of the LORD of Heaven's Armies on his day of intense rage. People will scatter and try to find their own little groups, like scared deer or lost sheep without a shepherd. They'll run for any shelter they can find. But it's bad news for anyone left behind—they'll be killed right where they stand, their throats slit and their stomachs cut open. Babies will be smashed against rocks while their parents watch, houses will be robbed, and wives will be assaulted."

"And now, watch this. I'm sending the Medes to attack Babylon. They're a savage crew that doesn't care about money; you can't buy them off. They'll slaughter the young people and have no problem killing even babies. And Babylon, the most magnificent of all kingdoms, the pride and joy of its people, will end up a smoking, stinking ruin, just like Sodom and Gomorrah after God was done with them. No one will ever live there again; it'll be a ghost town for generations. Not even nomads will set up camp there. Shepherds will stay far away. But it'll be a hotspot for weird, wild animals. They'll fill the empty houses with creepy noises at night. Skunks will move in, and terrifying creatures will haunt the place. The sound of hyenas laughing will make your skin crawl, and the howling of coyotes will give you major chills." "Babylon is toast. It's all going down soon."

title: The King of Babylon's Epic Fail
paragraphs: But it's a different story for Jacob's crew. God's gonna have their back and choose Israel again. He'll get them settled in their own land, and people from other places will see what's up and want to join them. The nations that were living there will even help them get back home. Then, plot twist, Israel will make slaves out of them in God's country, capturing the ones who captured them and ruling over the ones who gave them a hard time.

Once God gives you a break from all the drama, the trouble, and the rough life you had to live, you can taunt the king of Babylon with this song: No way, the bully is actually gone? The whole mean regime is over? God totally wrecked the rule of the wicked, the power of those tyrants who were always crushing people. It was like a non-stop storm of cruelty, a super angry rule full of torture and chasing people down.

But now it's all over. The whole world is just chilling and quiet. So let's get loud! Sing it out! The big pine trees are stoked, and the giant cedars of Lebanon are like, 'Phew, since you got chopped down, nobody's trying to chop us down anymore.' Even the dead people in the underworld are hyped, getting ready to welcome you when you show up. All the famous dead people and the old kings are gonna stand up and be like, 'Whoa, look who's weak like us now! Welcome to the club, buddy!'
So this is what all your fancy parties and music got you, Babylon. A one-way ticket to your own private room in the underworld, with a king-size bed of maggots and a blanket of worms. Gross.
What a fall from the top, O Babylon! You, the 'morning star,' the 'son of the dawn.' Now you're face down in the mud of the underworld, the same guy who used to flatten whole nations.

You were telling yourself, 'I'm gonna climb up to heaven. I'll put my throne above God's stars. I'll be the boss of the angel meetings on the holy mountain. I'll go higher than the clouds. I'll be the king of the whole universe!'

But you totally failed, didn't you? Instead of going up, you went way down—down with the dead, to the very bottom of the pit. People are just gonna stare at you and be like, 'Is this really the guy who scared the whole world and its kingdoms, who wrecked the earth and its cities, and who locked up his prisoners for life?'

Other kings get a nice funeral, with people saying good things about them and putting them in a fancy tomb. But you? You get tossed in a ditch like a dead animal, covered in rotting bodies. No fancy funeral for you! You ruined your own country and killed so many people. Nobody's even gonna remember your evil kids. They’re done for.
Get ready to take out the sons of that wicked king and his whole family line. No way they should ever own any land or mess up the world with their cities.

'I'm coming for them,' says God-of-the-Angel-Armies, 'and I'm gonna wipe out Babylon's name, its survivors, its kids, and its grandkids.' That's God's promise. 'I'll turn it into a nasty swamp and give it to the hedgehogs. Then I'll just erase it.' That's the decree of God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

God-of-the-Angel-Armies says: 'It's gonna happen exactly like I planned. I'm gonna crush the Assyrian who's trespassing on my land and stomp him into the ground on my mountains. I'll stop him from taking slaves and lift that heavy weight off of everyone.' This is the plan for the whole world, and this is the hand that's gonna do it, reaching into every single nation. God-of-the-Angel-Armies has a plan. Who's gonna cancel it? His hand is reached out. Who's gonna stop him?

In the year that King Ahaz died, this message came: Philistines, don’t get too excited just because your mean boss is gone. From that dead snake, a way worse snake is gonna come, and from that one, an even worse one. The poor people won't have to stress, and the needy will be safe. But you Philistines are gonna get hit with a famine, and whoever doesn't starve, God will take out. So cry and scream, you proud city! Freak out, Philistia! Look north, there's smoke from burning cities. A super tough and disciplined army is on its way.
So what do you say when people from other places ask what's going on? Tell them, 'God has set up Zion. The people who are poor and in trouble can find a safe place there.'

title: Moab is Canceled
paragraphs: A message about Moab: Dude, Ar of Moab? Totally wrecked. Gone in one night. Kir of Moab? Same story, wiped out overnight. The people of Dibon are climbing up to their hilltop chapel to cry their eyes out. Moab is just weeping over Nebo and Medba. Everyone's shaving their heads and beards—it's a whole vibe of mourning. They're all in the streets wearing black, on the roofs, in the town square... just tears everywhere. Total grief. Heshbon and Elealeh are wailing so loud you can hear them all the way in Jahaz. Moab is just sobbing, legit shaking. The soul of Moab is trembling.

Man, my heart breaks for Moab. Refugees are pouring into Zoar and then trying to get to Eglath-shelishiyah. They're weeping as they go up the slopes of Luhith, and on the road to Horonaim, they're crying about everything they've lost. The springs of Nimrim are bone dry—the grass is brown, the plants are dead, nothing's growing. So they're packing up everything they own and carrying it on their backs, trying to get across Willow Creek to safety. The sound of crying is echoing all over Moab, like, gut-wrenching sobs as far as Eglaim, and heart-breaking cries all the way to Beer-elim. The riverbanks of the Dibon are red with blood, but God's not done with Dibon yet. He's sending a lion to finish off the survivors, to clean up anyone left in the land.

title: Moab's Pride Gets Wrecked
paragraphs: Moab is basically saying, "Yo, send a bunch of lambs as a gift to the leaders in Jerusalem. Like, lambs from Sela, all the way across the desert, just to get on Jerusalem's good side." The people in Moab are totally lost, like baby birds that got kicked out of their nest, just flapping around helplessly by the Arnon River, stuck. They're crying out, "Someone tell us what to do, for real! Help us! Hide us! Let the refugees from Moab crash with you. Be a safe spot for us, we're running from a warzone."

And Judah hits back with, "Look, when all this drama is over, when the evil ruler is taken down, the fighting stops, and all this messed-up stuff is just a bad memory, a new government based on love is gonna be set up, just like in the good old days of King David. There's gonna be a leader you can actually count on, someone who's all about justice and making things right, ASAP."

Okay, so we've all heard about Moab's pride. They’re world-famous for it—super arrogant, think they're all that, just unbearable and full of hot air. So now it's Moab's turn to cry about it for a change, with all the neighbors throwing shade. What a shame! So tragic! No more of those fancy fruitcakes and Kir-hareseth candies. All those amazing fields in Heshbon are dried up, and the awesome vineyards in Sibmah are dead. Some foreign thugs came in and just wrecked the famous grapevines that used to stretch all the way to Jazer, right to the edge of the desert. They ripped up crops everywhere, as far as you can see. I'm gonna cry too. I'll cry with Jazer for the Sibmah vineyards. And yeah, Heshbon and Elealeh, I'm crying with you guys. The happy harvest parties are gone. Instead of singing and celebrating, it's just dead silent. No more laughing in the orchards, no more singing while you work in the vineyards. Instead of all the noise of good work being done, it's just silence—a super creepy, dead silence. My heart is breaking for Moab, my soul feels for sad Kir-heres. When Moab drags himself to the shrine to pray, it's a total waste of time and energy. Going to the sanctuary and praying for help is pointless. Nothing happens.

This was God's original message about Moab. But here's the update from God: "In three years, like, the same amount of time as a soldier's contract, Moab's whole impressive vibe will be gone. That big hot-air balloon of pride will be popped, and instead of a ton of people, there will just be a few broke dudes shuffling around, begging for handouts."

title: God vs. Everybody: The Ultimate Takedown
paragraphs: Check this out: Damascus is about to get wrecked. Like, totally leveled, just a pile of dust. All its towns will be ghost towns. Sheep and goats are gonna move in and act like they own the place... which they will. Ephraim's defenses? Gone. Damascus's government? Poof, vanished. And what's left of Aram will be the same as what's left of Israel—basically nothing. That's the word from the God of Heaven's Armies.

The time is coming when Jacob, who's been living large, is gonna look real rough, and his healthy bod will get super skinny. The whole country will be empty, like a field that's been completely picked over. It'll be like just a few stalks of grain left after the harvest, or like a couple of olives missed at the very top of the tree, or those four or five apples nobody could reach. That's a promise from the God of Israel.

For real, the day is coming when people will finally pay attention to their Creator and take a good, long look at the Holy One of Israel. They'll totally lose interest in all the stuff they made themselves—all their altars, statues, and rituals. Their whole DIY religion, no matter how cool it seems, will just be... meh.

And yeah, a time is coming when their super-strong cities will be completely abandoned—just like the cities the Hivites and Amorites ditched when Israel rolled in. The whole land will be empty and desolate.

And why's all this happening? Because you forgot about God, your Savior. You didn't remember the Rock who's your safe place. So, even though you're super religious, planting all these special gardens for your fake gods, and even though you get them to grow like crazy, with buds and flowers everywhere, it's all for nothing. Instead of a harvest, you're just gonna get a whole lot of pain and suffering. That’s rough.

Whoa, listen to that! It's the sound of a massive crowd of people, thundering like a huge ocean wave! Nations are roaring like a giant waterfall. But God's just gonna say one word and shut them all up. Then he'll blow them away like dead leaves in the wind, or like fluff from a thistle.
At night, it's pure terror. But by morning, it's all gone. Not a trace. That's what happens to anyone who tries to mess with us. That's the fate of those who are out to get us.

title: God's Surprise Pruning Job
paragraphs: Listen: there’s this land way out past Ethiopia, buzzing with bugs, and they're sending messengers all over the place, crossing rivers and oceans. These messengers are told to go to this nation of tall, good-looking people. Everyone respects them, they're super powerful and don't mess around. Their country is full of rivers.
Everyone on earth, listen up! When you see a flag on a mountain, pay attention. When you hear a trumpet, listen close.

Because God told me this: 'I'm just gonna chill and watch from my place. Quiet like the sun's warmth, silent like the morning dew during harvest.' But then, right before the harvest, when the flowers have turned into grapes, He's gonna step in. He'll chop off the new branches, and just go to town on the growing parts. He'll leave them on the ground for the birds and animals to eat all summer and winter.

Then, everyone from that nation of tall, good-looking people, the ones everyone used to respect, the powerful and relentless ones from the land of rivers, will bring gifts to God on Mount Zion, his special place.

title: Egypt's Ultimate Glow-Up Story
paragraphs: A message about Egypt: Check this out! God is rolling up on Egypt, riding a super-fast cloud. All of Egypt's fake gods are shaking in their boots, and the people are totally freaking out.

God's like, 'I'm gonna make Egyptians turn on each other. Brothers fighting brothers, neighbors fighting neighbors, cities against cities, kingdoms against kingdoms. It's gonna be pure chaos. I'll mess them up so bad they won't know what hit 'em. They'll be running to their fake gods and trying to talk to ghosts for answers, but it won't work. Then, I'm gonna hand them over to a seriously cruel dictator, a merciless king who will rule over them.' That's the word from the ultimate boss, God-of-the-Angel-Armies.

The Nile River is gonna dry up completely, the riverbed will be just baked earth. The canals will get all gross and smelly, and all the streams that feed the Nile will dry up too. All the plants along the river will die, and the whole area will be a wasteland. The fishermen will be complaining because there are no fish, and all the people who work with fabrics—weavers, cotton and wool workers—will lose their jobs. Everyone will be bummed out and unemployed.

The leaders of Zoan are a bunch of fools, and Pharaoh's advisors are just plain stupid. How can any of you even say to Pharaoh, 'Trust me, I'm smart, I know what's up. I come from a long line of wise Egyptians'? There's not a single wise person left in the whole country. If there were, they'd tell you what God-of-the-Angel-Armies has planned for Egypt. But nope, the leaders of Zoan are clueless, and the leaders of Memphis are idiots. The so-called 'pillars' of your society have led Egypt down a dead-end street. God has totally messed with their heads, and now Egypt is like a drunk person stumbling in their own vomit. Egypt is a lost cause, a hopeless old fool.

On that day, the Egyptians will be like scared little kids, screaming at every little thing God-of-the-Angel-Armies does. Just mentioning Judah will terrify them. The name itself will make them panic because they'll remember God's plan against Egypt.

On that day, a bunch of cities in Egypt will start speaking the language of faith and will promise to follow God-of-the-Angel-Armies. One of these cities will even get the cool name 'City of the Sun.'

On that day, there will be a place of worship to God right in the middle of Egypt and a monument to him at the border. It will be a sign of how God-of-the-Angel-Armies helped the Egyptians. When they cry out to God because of their problems, he'll send a savior to rescue and protect them. God will reveal himself to the Egyptians, and they will finally get to know him. They'll worship him for real, with sacrifices and offerings. They'll make promises to God and actually keep them. God will strike Egypt, but then he'll heal them. Egypt will come back to God, and he will hear their prayers and heal them completely.
On that day, there will be a highway connecting Egypt and Assyria. Assyrians will be able to hang out in Egypt, and Egyptians in Assyria. They won't be enemies anymore; they'll worship together!

On that day, Israel will join Egypt and Assyria, and they will all be a blessing to the world. God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who blessed Israel, will bless them all, saying, 'Blessed be Egypt, my people! Blessed be Assyria, my creation! And blessed be Israel, my special inheritance!'

title: Isaiah's "Naked Truth" Protest Goes Viral
paragraphs: So, back in the year when the top general sent by King Sargon of Assyria came to Ashdod, fought it, and took it over, God told Isaiah, son of Amoz, something pretty wild. He was like, "Go, take off your clothes and sandals." And Isaiah actually did it, just walking around naked and barefoot.

Then God explained, "Just like my servant Isaiah has been walking around naked and barefoot for three years as a huge warning sign to Egypt and Ethiopia, the king of Assyria is about to roll in and do the same to them. He's going to take the Egyptians as captives and the Ethiopians as exiles. He’ll march everyone out, young and old, totally naked and barefoot, for everyone to see—Egypt exposed and shamed. Everyone who was counting on Ethiopia and expecting Egypt to have their back is going to be totally shocked and confused. All the people living along the coast will be saying, 'Man, look at them! Naked and barefoot, getting dragged off into exile! We really thought they were our best hope to get saved from the king of Assyria. What are we supposed to do now? How are we ever going to get out of this?'"

title: Isaiah's Vision: The Fall of Babylon & Other Nations
paragraphs: A message about the desert by the sea: It's like when storms rip through the Negev desert, coming from that terrifying, empty place. I was shown a heavy vision: the betrayer gets betrayed, the destroyer gets destroyed. Elam, go attack! Media, lay siege! Persians, attack! Babylon, attack! I'm putting an end to all the groaning. This vision has me doubled over in pain, like a woman in labor. I'm shook by what I hear, and wrecked by what I see. I'm completely stunned and horrified. I was hoping for a chill evening, but it's turned into a total nightmare.
The fancy dinner is all set up, the guests are kicking back, eating and drinking, having a great time. Then suddenly, the call goes out: 'Princes, to your weapons! It's time to fight!'

This is what the Lord told me: 'Go, set up a lookout. Have him report everything he sees. When he spots chariots, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, and riders on camels, tell him to pay close attention, to listen for every little whisper.' Then the lookout shouts, 'Sir, I'm at my post, day and night, never leaving. And look, here they come! Chariots and horsemen in pairs!' Then a voice calls out: 'Babylon has fallen, has fallen! All the statues of her gods are smashed on the ground.'
My people, you who have been crushed and trampled, I'm telling you what I've heard from the Lord of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel.

A message about Edom: Someone calls to me from Seir, 'Watchman, what's left of the night? Watchman, what's left of the night?' The watchman replies, 'Morning is coming, but it's still night. If you want to ask again, go ahead.'

A message about Arabia: You caravans of Dedanites, you'll be camping in the wilderness of Arabia. You people of Tema, bring water for the thirsty, bring food for the refugees. They're running from the sword, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
This is what the Lord says to me: 'In exactly one year, all the glory of Kedar will be gone. The number of archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.' The Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.

title: God Fires a Corrupt Official, Promotes His Guy
paragraphs: A message about Vision Valley: Seriously, what is even happening here? All this wild partying and noise, everyone shouting and cheering in the streets, the whole city is just one big celebration. But like, you don't have any brave soldiers to be hyping up, no war heroes to be proud of. Your leaders were all total cowards, getting captured without even putting up a fight. A whole country of cowards, caught while trying to run away from the battle.

In the middle of all the shouting, I was like, “Just leave me alone. Let me just be sad by myself.” Don't try to tell me it's gonna be okay. These people are toast. It is not okay. Because the Boss, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, is bringing a day full of chaos, people pushing and stampeding in Vision Valley, knocking down walls and screaming to the mountains, “Attack! Attack!” Your old enemies Elam and Kir show up armed to the teeth—weapons, chariots, and cavalry. Your beautiful valleys are just loud with war, chariots and cavalry charging all over the place. God has left Judah totally exposed and defenseless.

On that day, you checked out your defenses, looked over your weapons in the Forest Armory. You found all the weak spots in the city walls that needed fixing. You made sure you had water from the Lower Pool. You went through all the houses in Jerusalem and tore some down to get bricks to make the city wall stronger. You even built a huge tank to make sure you had tons of water. You looked at everything, you checked everything, but you never once looked to the One who gave you this city in the first place. You never even thought to ask the One who had this whole thing planned out for a long time.

The Boss, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, called for that Day to be a day of crying and repentance, a day to wear sad, mourning clothes. But what did you do? You threw a party! Eating, drinking, and dancing in the streets! You're grilling up bulls and sheep and having a massive feast—huge slabs of meat, barrels of beer. "Eat and drink! We're all gonna die tomorrow anyway!"
God-of-the-Angel-Armies whispered his judgment on this whole party vibe to me: “You will pay for this nonsense until the day you die.” The Boss, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, said so.

The Boss, God-of-the-Angel-Armies, said: “Alright, go to this manager, Shebna, the guy in charge of the king's whole palace, and tell him: What are you even doing here? You're not from around here, but you act like you own the place, building a huge, fancy tomb for yourself where everyone can see it, making sure everyone thinks you're a big deal. Well, God is about to totally wreck you, throw you out. He’s gonna grab you, spin you around like crazy, and then just launch you like a ball until you're gone. Where you land, who knows. And you'll die there, with all the fancy stuff you collected piled on your grave. You've been a total disgrace to your master's house! You're fired—and honestly, good riddance!

“On that Day, I’ll replace Shebna. I will call my guy Eliakim, son of Hilkiah. I’ll give him your fancy robe. I’ll put your belt on him. I’ll give him your power. He’ll be like a father-figure to Jerusalem and the government of Judah. I’ll give him the key to King David's legacy. He'll have full access—he can open any door and it stays open, lock any door and it stays locked. I’ll set him in place like a super-strong nail in a solid wall. He’ll make the Davidic tradition secure. Everything will depend on him—not just the future of David's family but also all the little details of running the house, right down to the cups and plates.

“And then the Day will come,” says God-of-the-Angel-Armies, “when that nail will get loose and fall out, break right out of that solid wall—and everything hanging on it will crash down with it.” That’s what’s gonna happen. God said so.

title: The Richest City in the World Goes BROKE
paragraphs: Wail, ships of Tarshish, you better cry it out, 'cause your home ports are completely wrecked. When the ships sailed back from Cyprus, they saw the total chaos. And you merchants from Sidon, living by the coast? Just be quiet. Your crews were out there on the ocean, hustling, making bank on grain from Egypt, like some global mega-corporation. But now, Sidon, you should be seriously embarrassed. The ocean itself is speaking up, like, 'I've never been a mom, never had kids, never watched them grow up. It was all just business, all about the money, the profits and losses.'
When Egypt hears what happened to Tyre, they're gonna be freaking out, totally losing it.

Go check out Tarshish, all you coastal people. Take a long, hard look and just let it all out, cry your eyes out. Is this the same city you remember being so full of life and energy, that ancient, famous place that was basically taking over the world with its business deals? So who's responsible for Tyre's downfall, the city that used to run the global market? Their business people were the big shots, the ones calling all the plays. But God, the commander of heavenly armies, he's the one who brought it all crashing down. He did it to expose how ugly pride really is and to pop all those over-inflated egos. So, ships of Tarshish, you might as well go home. There's nothing left for you here. God messed with the ocean and the trading business, throwing all the sea-faring nations into chaos. He ordered the destruction of all those coastal cities, the hubs of all that business. And God said, 'You've got nothing to be proud of anymore, Sidon. You're broke and empty. Thinking of starting over in Cyprus? Don't even bother. It's not gonna work out for you there either.'

Just look at Babylon. It's a total wasteland now. Assyria turned it into a desert, a place for wild animals to roam. They brought in their heavy-duty demolition gear, knocked down all the buildings, and left nothing behind but rubble.
So cry it out, ships of Tarshish, 'cause your awesome ports are toast.

For the next 70 years, basically a whole lifetime, everyone's gonna forget about Tyre. But after those 70 years, Tyre's gonna try to make a comeback, but it'll be like that sad song about the washed-up celebrity: 'Grab your guitar, walk around the city, you forgotten star. Sing your old hits, all those songs you used to sing. Maybe someone will finally remember you.'

After those 70 years, God's gonna check up on Tyre. And she'll go right back to her old ways, selling herself to whoever pays the most, doing business with anyone and everyone, no standards at all. But here's the crazy part: all the money she makes, every single penny, is gonna be given to God. It's not going into some offshore bank account. All her profits will be used to help out the people who know and serve God, making sure they have plenty of food and the best clothes.

title: The Earth is Officially Canceled
paragraphs: Danger ahead! God’s about to wreck the earth and leave it in ruins, tear everything up by the roots and send everyone running for their lives: priests and regular people, bosses and workers, celebs and nobodies, buyers and sellers, bankers and beggars, the rich and the poor—everyone’s included. The whole world is gonna look like a wasteland, completely trashed. And why? Because God said so. He gave the order.
The earth is looking grim and washed out, the world is silent and depressing, the sky and land are totally lifeless and bland.

The earth is polluted by the people living on it, who broke all the rules, messed up the natural order, and violated the sacred, eternal agreement. So now a curse is eating away at the earth like cancer. Its people are paying the price for their disrespect. They’re disappearing, dying off one by one. No more wine, no more vineyards, no more singing and celebrating. The sound of music is gone, the happy shouts are gone, the cheerful instruments are gone. No more parties with fancy drinks. Heavy drinkers can't even stomach their booze anymore. The chaotic cities are a mess. It's total anarchy. Every house is boarded up and condemned. People are rioting in the streets for wine, but the good times are officially over—no more joy for this world. The city is dead and abandoned, just piles of rubble. That’s what’s going to happen to the whole earth. This is the future for every nation: like an olive tree shaken clean of its olives, or a grapevine picked clean of its grapes.

But some people will start singing with joy. From the west, they’ll shout about how majestic God is. And from the east, God’s glory will rise. Every island in the sea will broadcast God’s fame, the fame of the God of Israel. From all over the world, we hear them singing: “All praise to the Righteous One!”

But I said, “That’s great for them, but all I see is doom, doom, and more doom.” Everyone is at each other’s throats, literally. There’s terror, traps, and pitfalls everywhere, no matter who you are. If you run from the terror, you’ll fall into a pit. If you climb out of the pit, you’ll get caught in a trap. Chaos is pouring down from the sky. The earth’s foundations are crumbling. The earth is smashed to pieces, ripped to shreds, and shaking uncontrollably. The earth is stumbling like a drunk person, swaying like a shack in a hurricane. Its mountain of sins is too heavy for it. It collapses and won’t get back up.

That’s when God will call out the rebel powers in the sky and the rebel kings on earth. They’ll be rounded up like prisoners, locked up in jail, and then sentenced to hard labor. The moon will be so ashamed it will hide, and the sun will be so humiliated it will turn away in disgrace, because God-of-the-Angel-Armies will take over, ruling from Mount Zion and Jerusalem, looking splendid and glorious in front of all his leaders.

title: God's Epic Victory Party!
paragraphs: God, you're my God. I’m here to celebrate you and praise your name. You've done some seriously amazing things, plans that were perfectly thought out and are 100% solid. You've turned that big city into a pile of rocks, the super strong city is just rubble now. The enemy's main city is basically deleted, it's never gonna be a city again. The world's superpowers will see it and give you respect, and those brutal bullies will bow down in awe. They'll see you've got the backs of the poor, that you're there for them when they're in trouble. You're like a warm, dry spot in a storm, and a cool, shady place when it's blazing hot. Those savage oppressors are like a crazy winter blizzard, and the fierce foreigners are like the scorching sun in the desert. But you, God, you're the shelter from the storm and the shade from the sun, you shut down those loud-mouthed bullies.

And right here on this mountain, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies is gonna throw a wild feast for everyone in the world. A feast with the best food, the best-aged wines, like a seven-course meal that's super fancy with gourmet desserts. And on this mountain, God's gonna get rid of that dark cloud of doom that's hanging over everyone, that shadow of death that's on all the nations. Yeah, he’s gonna banish death forever. And God will wipe away every single tear from every face. He'll take away all the shame and disgrace from his people, no matter where they are. For real! God said so!

When that time comes, people will be like, “Whoa, look what happened! This is our God! We waited for him and he actually showed up and saved us! This is the God we were waiting for! Let's party and celebrate the joy of him saving us. God's hand is protecting this mountain!”

But as for the Moabites, they're gonna get treated like actual garbage, like straw getting trampled into a manure pile. They can struggle all they want, like a swimmer trying not to drown, but they'll just sink in the sewage. Their own pride will drag them down. Their famous strong walls will totally crumble, those huge walls will just turn to dust.

title: God's Ultimate Comeback Plan
paragraphs: On that day, everyone in Judah will be singing this song: We've got this super strong city, basically 'Salvation City,' and its walls are made of, you guessed it, salvation. So open up the gates for all the good and real ones to come in. The people who keep their minds focused on you, God, you keep them totally secure and steady. They're not giving up, because they know they can count on you. Seriously, just trust God and keep going, because with God, it's a sure thing. All those arrogant people who thought they were all that? God knocked them right off their high horse. He took their fancy city on a hill and turned it into a swamp. And now, all the people who were stepped on and left out are building their new lives on that same land.

The path for people doing the right thing is totally smooth. God, the ultimate Leveler, makes the road even for them. We're not in a rush, God. We're cool with just chilling in the path you've laid out for us. Who you are and what you've done is literally all we could ever want. All night, my soul is just longing for you. Deep down, my spirit is reaching out for you. When your judgments are out there for everyone to see, people actually learn how to live right. But if you show grace to the wicked, they just don't get it. Even in a land of right living, they keep doing wrong, totally blind to how awesome you are, God.

You're holding your hand up high, God, but they're not even seeing it. Open their eyes to what you're doing, let them see the passionate love you have for your people. Make them feel ashamed. Light a fire under them. Get the attention of these haters of yours. God, please bring us a life that's peaceful and whole, because everything we've ever accomplished, you were the one who did it for us. Oh God, our God, we've had other 'masters' trying to rule us, but you're the only one we'll ever claim. The dead don't talk, and their ghosts don't haunt, because you basically said, 'Enough—that's all for you,' and just deleted them from existence. But the living? You make them larger than life. The more life you give, the more your glory shines, and you expand the borders to make room for even more life!

Oh God, they cried out to you for help when they were in deep trouble, when your discipline was so intense they could barely even whisper a prayer. It was like a woman giving birth, writhing and screaming in pain as the baby comes. That's what we were like because of you, O God. We were like, nine months pregnant, went through all the labor pains, but... no baby. We gave birth to nothing but wind. All our hard work was for nothing. We didn't produce anything that was alive. We couldn't save the world.

But listen up, my friends, your dead will live again. Your corpses will get back on their feet. All you who are dead and buried, wake up and sing! Your dew is like the morning dew that catches the first rays of sunlight, and the earth itself is bursting with life, giving birth to the dead.

So come on, my people, go home and lock yourselves in. Go into hiding for a little while until this wave of punishment is over. Because God is definitely coming out from his place to punish the evil that people on earth have done. The earth itself will expose the bloodstains; it will show everyone where the murdered have been hidden all this time.

title: God's Epic Takedown & Vineyard Comeback
paragraphs: On that day, God's gonna whip out his sword—a seriously huge and powerful one. He's going after Leviathan, that giant sea serpent, as it tries to get away. He's gonna take down that ancient dragon that lives in the ocean.

At the same time, this awesome vineyard will show up. Sing about it! God says, 'I'm the one taking care of it, making sure it has enough water. I'm watching over it so nothing can mess it up. I'm not mad at it. I actually care. Even if it grows some weeds, I'll just pull them out and get rid of them. This vine should hold on to me to be safe, to have a real and full life with me.'
The time is coming when Jacob's family will put down roots, and Israel will blossom and grow, filling the whole world with its fruit.

Has God wrecked them like he wrecked their enemies? Nah. Were they killed off the same way their killers were? Nope. He was tough on them, for sure. Getting exiled was a harsh punishment. He basically blew them away with a powerful wind. But the good news is, through all that, Jacob's guilt was erased. The proof that his sin is gone is this: he'll tear down all the fake altars, take them apart piece by piece, crush the stones, and get rid of all the weird religious shrines. Because that whole flashy setup is gone. Nobody lives there anymore. It's a ghost town. But, hey, animals are chilling there, eating and sleeping. It's also a decent spot to find firewood since there are plenty of dry branches. It's what's left of a people who had no clue about God. So the God who made them won't have anything to do with them. The one who created them will turn his back on them.

On that day, God will gather his people from the Euphrates River all the way to the Brook of Egypt. And you, the people of Israel, will be picked out one by one. A huge trumpet will sound, calling all the exiles home from Assyria and the refugees from Egypt. They'll all come to worship God on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

title: God's Wrecking Ball vs. Your Lame Insurance Plan
paragraphs: It's over for the show-off drunks of Ephraim. They're looking rough—a total mess. They used to be so impressive, but now they're just a bunch of sloppy, beer-bellied jokes. But watch out, 'cause God's got someone lined up to take them down. Someone seriously tough who's gonna wreck them. Like a crazy hailstorm or a hurricane, or a flash flood, he's gonna slam them to the ground with one hand. Samaria, that party hat on Israel's head? It's getting knocked right off. Gone faster than a snack you'd toss to your dog.

But for the people who are left, God of the Angel Armies will be a beautiful crown on their heads. He'll give wisdom and a sense of what's right to the leaders making the calls, and he'll give strength and skill to the ones protecting everyone.

And get this, even the priests and prophets are wasted. They’re stumbling around, completely drunk. So drunk on wine and whiskey they can't see straight or even talk right. Literally every table is covered in puke. They're living in their own filth. It's nasty.

They're like, 'For real? Who do you think you are, trying to teach us? Who are you to boss us around? We're not little kids. You can't talk down to us like we're babies— ‘goo goo ga ga, blah blah blah.’

But that's exactly how God's gonna talk to them. He's gonna use their enemies to speak to them in baby talk, one syllable at a time. He already told them, 'This is where you can chill, let the tired people rest. This is the spot to drop your stress.' But they just wouldn't listen.

So God's gonna start from square one, talking to them in baby talk, one syllable at a time— 'Da, da, da, da, blah, blah, blah, blah. Good job, little one.' And just like toddlers, they're gonna get up and fall flat on their faces, get all bruised and confused and totally lost.

Alright, listen up, you mockers, you guys who are in charge of the people in Jerusalem. You're all like, 'We're good, we've got a solid life insurance plan. We've covered all our bases. No disaster can even touch us. We've thought of everything, got the experts on our side. We're set.'

But the real boss, God, has something to say about that: 'Watch this. I'm laying a foundation in Zion, a legit, solid granite foundation. It's perfectly square and true. And here's what it means: if you trust in me, you won't get knocked over. I'm gonna use justice as my measuring tape and what's right as my level. A hailstorm is gonna tear down your little house of lies, and a flash flood will wash away all the trash.'

Then you'll see that your fancy life insurance policy was completely worthless. All your little plans to cheat death were just a bunch of lies and illusions. When the disaster hits, you're gonna be totally crushed by it. Every single time disaster comes, you'll be right in the middle of it—disaster in the morning, disaster at night. Every time you hear about another disaster, you'll be shaking in fear. There will be nowhere to rest, nothing to hide under. God's gonna stand up tall, as furious as he was way back on Mount Perazim and in the Gibeon valley against the Philistines. But this time, he's coming for you. It's hard to believe, but it's happening. Not what you expected, but it's coming. So get serious, guys, and stop scoffing. That's just gonna make it worse. I've heard the orders for destruction, straight from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies—and it's gonna be a worldwide disaster.

Now listen to me. Pay close attention. Do farmers just plow all day, every day? Or just break up the soil and do nothing else? Nah. After they get the ground ready, they plant stuff, right? They scatter dill and cumin, plant wheat and barley in the main fields, and put raspberries along the edges. They know exactly what to do and when. Their God taught them.

And when it's time to harvest, they're careful with the delicate stuff like dill and cumin. But the wheat gets threshed and milled, but not forever. The farmer knows how to handle each type of grain. He learned it all from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, who knows everything about when, how, and where.
