title: God's Wake-Up Call is No Joke
paragraphs: Doom to Ariel, the same city where King David set up his base. Go ahead, let the years pass, celebrate your holidays, but I'm about to bring the pain to Jerusalem. It's gonna be all moans and groans. To me, Jerusalem is an 'Ariel'—a lion of God, and I'm surrounding you just like David did. I'm setting up a siege, building towers, and rolling in the heavy artillery. You'll be so beat down, you'll be whispering from the dirt. Your voice will sound like a ghost's, mumbling from the dust.

But plot twist! Your enemies? They're the ones who are gonna get wrecked, turned into dust. That whole crew of bullies trying to mess with you will be gone in a flash, like dust in the wind. Because—surprise!—God of the Angel Armies is about to show up. We're talking thunder, earthquakes, and a crazy loud noise, plus hurricanes, tornadoes, and lightning. The whole mob of nations fighting Ariel, the ones causing all the drama? They'll just be a bad dream, a total nightmare. Like a starving guy dreaming of a massive feast and waking up still hungry, or a thirsty girl dreaming of chugging a giant iced tea and waking up with a dry mouth. That's how it'll be for all those nations fighting Mount Zion. They'll wake up and realize they didn't accomplish a single thing.

Go on, get wasted so you can't feel anything. Blind yourselves so you don't have to see. Get drunk, but not on alcohol. Pass out, but not from booze. God's the one who has put you in this deep, deep sleep. He's put your prophets and seers—the ones who are supposed to see what's coming—to sleep.

What you're being shown is like a sealed letter. If you give it to someone who can read and say, 'Hey, read this,' they'll just say, 'I can't, it's sealed.' And if you give it to someone who can't read and tell them to read it, they'll just say, 'Dude, I can't read.'

The Master said: 'These people talk a good game, saying all the right things, but their hearts are so not in it. They go through the motions of worship, but it's all fake. So, I'm about to step in and seriously shock them. It's gonna be wild. The so-called 'wise' ones who thought they had it all figured out will be exposed as clowns. The smarty-pants who acted like they knew everything will be shown up as knowing nothing.'

You're so done. You act like you've got some secret knowledge, cutting God out and making your own plans in the dark. You scheme about the future like you're in control, always being shady and never showing your cards. You've got it all backward! It's like a pot telling the potter he's just a lump of clay. Does a book say to its author, 'He didn't even write me'? Does a gourmet meal say to the chef, 'She had nothing to do with making this'?

And then, just like that, when you least expect it, and with you doing absolutely nothing, things will totally flip. The dead forests of Lebanon will turn into amazing gardens, and Mount Carmel will be covered in trees again. When that happens, the deaf will actually hear what's written down, word for word. After living in the dark their whole lives, the blind will finally see. The people who were always left out will be laughing and dancing for God, and the ones who were always down will be shouting praises to the Holy One of Israel. Because the street gangs will be gone. The haters and mockers will be a thing of the past. The people who were always looking for a chance to hurt others will be gone for good: the ones who messed with the courts, the ones who scammed the poor, and the ones who hurt innocent people.

And finally, this is God's message for Jacob's family, the same God who saved Abraham: 'Jacob won't have to be ashamed anymore, no more being pale and weak from waiting. Because he's going to see his kids, my personal gift to him—tons of kids. And these kids will honor me by living right. They'll worship the Holy One of Jacob and be in total awe of the God of Israel. The ones who were all messed up will get their act together, and the complainers and whiners will finally learn to be grateful.'

title: God's Plan vs. Your Plan
paragraphs: “Y'all are in deep trouble, you rebel kids,” God says. “You're making your own plans, not mine. You're shaking on deals that have nothing to do with my Spirit. You're just stacking up mistakes, one on top of the other, running off to Egypt without even checking with me first, thinking Pharaoh's got your back, that you can just chill in Egypt. Yeah, right. Like Pharaoh's gonna protect you. Like Egypt is some safe house. Sure, they talk a big game, with their officials posted up in Zoan and Hanes, but it's all for show. Anyone who actually falls for it is gonna look like a total fool. It’s all hype, no substance—a total embarrassment.”

And get this, about the animals in the Negev desert on the way to Egypt: that road is seriously dangerous, like, crawling with lions and poisonous snakes. And you're really gonna drag all your stuff down there, loading up your donkeys and camels with gifts, thinking you can buy protection from that joke of a country? Egypt is all talk. I'm calling it the 'Toothless Dragon'.

So, go write this all down. Put it in a book so future generations can learn from it. Because you guys are a bunch of rebels, total liars, who won't listen to a single thing God says. You're telling your pastors, 'Don't hit us with that irrelevant stuff.' You're telling your preachers, 'Don't waste our time with impractical things. Just tell us what we want to hear. Don't bore us with that old-school religion. That stuff is dead. Stop going on about 'The Holy One of Israel.''”

Because of that, the Holy One of Israel says this: “Since you're dissing this message and choosing to live a crooked and shady life, this whole messed-up lifestyle is gonna be like a huge, janky wall that's slowly leaning and cracking, and then boom—it all comes crashing down without warning. It'll be smashed into a million pieces like a clay pot, so broken you can't even use a piece of it. It'll just be a pile of junk to sweep up and throw away.”

God, the Master, the Holy One of Israel, gives this serious advice: “Your only way to be saved is to come back to me and stop trying so hard to save yourselves. Your real strength comes from chilling out and completely depending on me—but you're not having any of it. You're like, ‘Nah, we're gonna get on our horses and bolt!’ And you will bolt, alright—just not fast enough. You said, ‘We'll ride fast horses!’ You think the guys chasing you are on slow ponies? Think again. A thousand of you will scatter from just one enemy. Five of them will make you all run for it. There'll be nothing left of you—like a flagpole on a hill with no flag, or a signpost with no sign.”
But God's not done. He's waiting to be good to you. He's gearing up to show you mercy. God does everything right, at the right time. If you wait for him, you're the lucky ones.

For real, people of Zion, citizens of Jerusalem, you can stop crying. Cry out for help, and you'll get grace on grace. The second he hears you, he'll answer. Even though the Master let you go through hard times, he'll make sure your teacher is right there with you. Your teacher will be on the scene, in your town, keeping you on track. Whenever you start to drift left or right, you'll hear, “This is the right way. Walk this way.” You'll get rid of all your expensive, trendy idols. You'll toss them in the trash like they're garbage and say, “Good riddance!”

God will send rain for the seeds you plant. The crops you grow will be massive. Your cows will have tons of space to graze. The oxen and donkeys you use for work will be eating good, right next to fresh streams flowing from the mountains and hills, not even worried about wars or earthquakes. Even better, on the day God heals his people from all the hurt they went through, the moonlight will be as bright as the sun, and the sunlight will be like a whole week of sunshine packed into one day, flooding everything.

Look, God is coming, and he's coming from far away! He's smoking with anger, huge as he gets closer. His words are steaming, fiery, and accusing. It's a flood of words, a flash flood that pulls everyone in. He's going to shake up the nations and filter them out, leading them to a dead end.

But you guys will be singing, like you're at an all-night party for God. Your hearts will be so full of song, like the sound of flutes in a parade on the way to God's mountain, to the Rock of Israel. God's voice will boom like thunder, and he'll show off his powerful arm. He'll be furious, throwing off sparks—a massive storm with rain and hail. For real, Assyria will be terrified by God's thunder and the beatdown he's about to give them. Every hit God lands on them will be perfectly in time with the music of drums and pipes. God will be fighting them with everything he's got, a two-fisted battle. The fiery pit of Topheth is all set and ready for the Assyrian king. The furnace is deep and wide, stacked with wood, ready to burn hot. And God's breath, like a river of flaming tar, will be the one to light it all up.

title: Stop Trusting Horses, Start Trusting God
paragraphs: It’s a total disaster for anyone running to Egypt for backup, thinking their horses and chariots are the answer. They’re all hyped about the size of the army but won’t even give a second glance to the Holy God of Israel or bother with a single prayer. But here's the deal: God is truly wise and knows exactly what he’s doing. He can unleash chaos when He wants and He doesn't bluff. He steps in to shut down evil plans and stands up to anyone causing trouble. Remember, Egyptians are just people, not God. Their horses are just flesh and blood, not some divine spirit. When God decides to act, both the so-called helpers and those they're trying to help will all go down together and end up in the same dirt pile.

God told me this: “I'm like a lion, the king of the jungle, totally focused on its meal, not even bothered by a bunch of shepherds trying to scare it away. That’s how I, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, will come down to fight for Mount Zion and take charge from its heights. And like a massive eagle hovering protectively in the sky, I, the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, will shield Jerusalem. You better believe I’ll protect and rescue it. I’ll watch over it and deliver it.”

So turn back, dear Israel, and come back to the One you so cruelly ditched. The day you finally decide to return, every single one of you will toss out those worthless idols you crafted with your own sinful hands.

“The Assyrians will be struck down, but not by a human sword. A sword not wielded by any person will finish them. They will flee from that sword, running for their lives, and their best young warriors will be taken as slaves. In sheer terror, their 'rock-solid' nation will crumble to pieces, and their leaders will scatter in a complete panic.” This is God's official decree on Assyria. His fire is blazing in Zion, His furnace is burning hot in Jerusalem.

title: The King We've All Been Waiting For
paragraphs: Check it out! A legit king is gonna rule the right way, and his crew will make sure things are fair. Each of them will be like a shield from the crazy winds, a safe spot when the storms hit. They'll be like a cool stream in a dry desert, or a huge rock giving shade when it's blazing hot. Anyone who looks will actually see, and anyone who listens will actually hear. The impulsive peeps will start making smart choices, and those who stumble over their words will speak clearly and well. No more will idiots get famous, or cheaters get all the credit. 'Cause fools are just fools, always cooking up new ways to cause trouble. They mess up people's lives and spread lies about God, totally ignoring the homeless and hungry, and not caring about those who are thirsty. And the crooks? They're sneaky and always finding new ways to sin and create drama, taking advantage of the poor with their scams and lies, not even batting an eye at the people they're hurting. But the real ones, the noble ones, they make good plans and always stand for what's right.

Alright, listen up, all you lazy ladies! All you spoiled, do-nothing women, pay attention to what I'm about to say. In just a little over a year, your chill lives are gonna get rocked. The grape harvest is gonna fail, and there won't be any fruit on the trees. So you better tremble, you idle women. Get serious, you pampered dolls! Strip down and discard your silk fineries. Put on funeral clothes. Shed honest tears for the lost harvest, the failed vintage. Weep for my people’s gardens and farms that grow nothing but thistles and thornbushes. Cry tears, real tears, for the happy homes no longer happy, the merry city no longer merry. The royal palace is deserted, the bustling city quiet as a morgue, The emptied parks and playgrounds taken over by wild animals, delighted with their new home.

Yeah, go ahead and cry and be sad until the Spirit comes down on us from heaven. Then the dry desert will grow crops, and the good fields will turn into forests. Justice will finally come to the desert, and what's right will make its home in the fertile fields. And when there's righteousness, there will be peace. The result of doing right will be quiet lives and endless trust. My people will live in a peaceful place—in safe homes, in quiet gardens. The forest of your pride will be chopped down, and the city that shows off your power will be destroyed. But you will have a blessed life, planting fields and gardens with plenty of water, and your animals will graze freely.

title: God's Epic Comeback & The Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: Man, it's over for you, Mr. Destroyer, who hasn't been destroyed yet. And you, Mr. Betrayer, who hasn't been betrayed. Once you're done destroying, it's your turn to get wrecked. Once you're done betraying, it's your turn to get betrayed.

God, be nice to us. You're literally our only hope. Be there for us first thing in the morning. When stuff gets real, help us out. You just had to say the word and everyone bounced. You showed up and whole nations scattered. And for once, your people got to grab the loot, clearing out all the enemy's stuff.

God is on another level, seriously. He's holding it all together. Zion is just overflowing with what's fair and right. God keeps your life stable and secure—giving you tons of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. And the best part? Zion's ultimate treasure: respecting God.

But for real, look! Listen! The tough guys are straight up crying. The diplomats who were supposed to make peace are in tears. The roads are empty—nobody's out there. The peace treaty is trash, they broke all the rules, and the people who signed it are getting dissed. The ground is mourning, the mountains of Lebanon are sad, the flower fields of Sharon are a mess of weeds, and the forests of Bashan and Carmel are just bare branches.

"Alright, I'm stepping in now," God says. "From now on, I'm in charge. No more playing nice. Now you'll see how powerful I am. You guys are nothing. You think you're making something big, but it's just useless fluff. You're full of hot air and you're just gonna self-destruct. You’re only good for being fertilizer and firewood."

"If you're far away, take note of what I’ve done. And if you're close by, pay attention to my track record. The sinners in Zion are freaking out, and for good reason. The godless are at their breaking point, like, 'Who can even survive this crazy fire? Who can get through this purge alive?'"

The answer is actually simple: Live right, tell the truth, hate it when people get taken advantage of, say no to bribes, reject violence, and stay away from trashy entertainment. That's how you level up your life! A safe and stable way to live. A fulfilling and satisfying way to live.

Oh, you'll see the king—and it'll be an amazing sight. You'll see these huge, wide-open lands. You'll think back on the old scary times and be like, "What happened to that Assyrian inspector who was always taking our stuff? And the guy who taxed us like crazy? And that scammer who cheated us with money?" Gone! You'll never see them again. Their disrespect is just a faint memory now. No more having to listen to a language you can't even understand, no more gibberish in your ears.

Just look at Zion, for real. It's the center of our worship, with all its festivals! Just feast your eyes on Jerusalem, a chill and permanent place to live. No more packing up and moving all the time, no more living in janky tents. Instead, you get God! The majestic God, God himself is our place, in a land with huge rivers and streams. But these rivers are blocked off to enemy ships, no pirate raids allowed. Because God makes all the calls here. God is our king. God runs this place and he'll keep us safe.

Ha! Your sails are all torn up, your mast is about to fall over, and your ship is leaking. The loot is just sitting there for anyone to take, for real—for the weak and the strong, insiders and outsiders.
No one in Zion will say, "I'm sick." And best of all, they'll all live without feeling guilty.

title: God's Judgment Day is NO JOKE
paragraphs: Alright, listen up, everyone! All you nations, get over here and pay attention. Yeah, you too, Earth, and everything on it. The whole world, and everyone in it.

And here’s the deal: God is seriously ticked off at all the nations. He's so mad at their armies that He's about to just delete them from the planet. Their bodies will be piled up and smell worse than a landfill in August, and their blood will be flowing down mountains like a crazy spring flood. The stars are gonna fall out of the sky like old, mushy fruit, and the sky itself will get folded up and stored away. That whole army of stars? Gone. Just like dead leaves in the fall.

God's like, "After I'm done with the sky and the earth, I'm coming for Edom. I'm gonna bring the hammer down on them, a people I've decided to totally wipe out." God's got a sword, and it's thirsty for blood. It's hungry for well-fed flesh—lambs, goats, the works. Yep, God's planned a huge sacrifice in Bozrah, their capital. The whole country of Edom is gonna be like a slaughterhouse. It's a massive slaughter of all animals, wild and farm alike. The whole place will be soaked in blood and greasy with fat.

This is God's official time for payback, the year He settles all of Zion's scores. Edom's rivers will get all thick and nasty with pollution, and the ground will be poisoned and useless. The whole country will be a smoking, stinking garbage fire that never goes out, day or night. It'll be a wasteland for generations—nobody's gonna be traveling through there anymore. Vultures and skunks will be running the streets, and owls and crows will move in. God's gonna hit the undo button on creation. Total chaos. No more life. Just emptiness. Their leaders will have no one to rule over. They'll call it 'No Kingdom Here,' a place where all the royalty is out of a job. Weeds will take over the castles, and wild dogs will roam the ruins. Wildcats and hyenas will team up to hunt, and demons and devils will dance through the night. The demon Lilith will even set up her permanent home there. It's gonna be a breeding ground for all kinds of creepy, evil stuff.

Go and read God's book. None of this is just gonna disappear. This evil has been commanded by God Himself. His Spirit made it happen. He's given them their place and decided their fate. This is forever. Generation after generation, it's the same story.

title: The Ultimate Glo-Up is Coming!
paragraphs: The middle-of-nowhere desert is about to have a major party. The dry, boring lands will be celebrating and blooming with flowers, just like crocuses in the spring. It's gonna be an explosion of color and song. Think of the most beautiful mountains you've ever seen, like Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon—all their beauty will be on display, showing off how awesome and majestic God is.

So, tell your tired friends to get some energy and your shaky friends to stand strong. Tell anyone who's scared, 'Don't worry! God is on His way to make everything right. He's coming to fix all the bad stuff and save you!'

When He shows up, it’s gonna be amazing. People who were blind will be able to see, and those who were deaf will hear everything. People who couldn't walk will be jumping around like deer, and those who couldn't speak will be singing their hearts out. Water will start flowing in the driest places, turning hot sand into a cool, refreshing oasis, and thirsty ground into a splashing fountain. Even the wild animals will have plenty to drink, and the dead grasslands will become super lush.

There's gonna be a special highway called the 'Holy Road.' No rude or rebellious people are allowed on it; it's exclusively for God's crew. You literally can't get lost on this road—even a total fool could find their way. There won't be any lions or other dangerous animals, so it's completely safe. Only the people God has saved will be walking on it. They'll be singing as they head home to Zion, glowing with a joy that never fades. They'll be welcomed home with so much happiness that all their sadness and worries will just disappear into the night.

title: Assyria's King Tries to Cancel Hezekiah
paragraphs: So, in King Hezekiah's fourteenth year, King Sennacherib of Assyria rolled up on all of Judah's fortified cities and just took them. Then the Assyrian king sent his top general, the 'Rabshekah,' with a massive army from Lachish to Jerusalem to confront King Hezekiah. The general posted up at the aqueduct by the upper pool, right on the road to the public laundry. Three of Hezekiah's guys went out to meet him: Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace; Shebna, the secretary; and Joah, the official historian.

The Rabshekah told them, 'Go tell Hezekiah that the Great King, the king of Assyria, is asking: ‘Who do you think is gonna have your back against me? You're all talk, and I'm calling you out. Your words are nothing against my army. Who's your backup now that you've decided to rebel? Egypt? Ha. Trusting Egypt is like leaning on a wet noodle. You'll just end up on the ground. That's all Pharaoh is to anyone who trusts him. And if you're about to say, ‘We’re trusting in our God,’ isn't it a little late for that? Didn't Hezekiah just tear down all the worship spots, telling everyone, ‘You have to worship at *this* altar’?'

'For real, be smart about this. My boss, the king of Assyria, will give you 2,000 horses if you can even find guys to ride them. You can't, can you? So how do you think you can stand up to even the lowest-ranking officer in my master's army, especially when you're depending on Egypt's weak chariots and riders?'
'And for real, do you think I came all this way to wreck this place without God's okay? It was your God who told me, ‘Go attack this land. Destroy it.’'
Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah were like, 'Hey, can you please talk to us in Aramaic? We get that. Don't speak Hebrew where all these people can hear you.'

But the Rabshekah shot back, 'You think my master sent me to talk to just you and your boss? Nah, this message is for everyone sitting on that wall. They're the ones who are gonna end up eating their own excrement and drinking their own urine.'

Then the Rabshekah stood up and yelled out in Hebrew, so everyone could understand, 'Listen up to the message from the Great King, the king of Assyria! Don't buy Hezekiah's lies. He can't save you. And don't listen to Hezekiah's religious talks telling you to trust God, saying ‘God will save us, for sure. God won’t let this city get taken by the king of Assyria.’'

'Don't listen to Hezekiah. Listen to what the king of Assyria is offering: ‘Make peace with me. Surrender. Everyone will get a good life, with their own land and water, and down the road, something even better. I’ll move you to a wide-open space, with more than enough good land for everyone.’ Don't let Hezekiah fool you with his lies that ‘God will save us.’ Has that ever actually happened? Has any god ever beaten the king of Assyria? Look around. Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? The gods of Sepharvaim? Did their gods do anything for Samaria? Name one god that has ever saved its country from me. So what makes you think your God can save Jerusalem from me?'
The three officials were totally silent. They didn't say a word, because the king had told them, 'Don't answer him.'

Then Eliakim, the palace manager, Shebna, the secretary, and Joah, the court historian, tore their clothes because they were so defeated and upset. They went back and told Hezekiah everything the Rabshekah had said.

title: God's Ultimate Clapback
paragraphs: When King Hezekiah got the news, he totally freaked out. He ripped his clothes, put on some scratchy burlap sacks to show how sorry he was, and went straight to God's temple. He sent his top guys—Eliakim, the palace manager; Shebna, the secretary; and the head priests, all wearing the same uncomfortable burlap—to find the prophet Isaiah.

They told him, "Hezekiah is saying, 'This is a dark day. We're in a major crisis. It feels like we're about to give birth but have zero strength left.' Do you think your God heard all the trash talk from the Rabshekah, who was sent by the Assyrian king to diss the living God? And is God gonna do something about it? Please, Isaiah, pray for us. Pray for the few of us who are left."

When they got to Isaiah, he said, "Go back and tell your boss this: 'God says, Don’t even sweat what you heard. All that smack talk from the Assyrian king’s little servants? I got this. I'm gonna plant a rumor in his ear that'll make him rush back home. And right there, in his own country, he’s gonna die a violent death.'"
The Rabshekah bounced and found the Assyrian king busy fighting another town, Libnah, because he'd heard the king had left Lachish.

Right then, the Assyrian king gets an urgent message about King Tirhakah of Ethiopia: "He's marching out to fight you." Hearing that, he fires off another message to Hezekiah: "Don't let your God, who you're so blindly trusting, fool you by promising Jerusalem won't fall to me. Get real! Look at what the kings of Assyria have done all over the world—we've wrecked country after country. You think you're special? Did any of the gods of those nations we destroyed—Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, the people of Eden—lift a finger to save them? Look around. See any trace of the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, or Ivvah? Didn't think so."
Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers and read it. Then he went back to God's temple, laid the letter out for God to see, and prayed.

Hezekiah prayed, "God of the Angel Armies, the one who rules from above the angels, you are the one and only God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth. God, please listen. Look at this. See all this hate that Sennacherib is spewing to mock you, the living God. And yeah, it's true, God, the Assyrian kings have totally destroyed all those nations and their lands. They threw their gods in the fire—which, let's be real, wasn't a big deal since they were fake gods anyway, just wood and stone statues. So, of course, they were destroyed. But now, our God, please step in. Save us from him. Let every kingdom on earth know that you, and only you, are the real God."

Then Isaiah sent a message back to Hezekiah: "This is what God, the God of Israel, says: Because you came to me about King Sennacherib of Assyria, here's my answer. "'She's not impressed with you, Sennacherib. The virgin daughter Zion thinks you're a joke. Daughter Jerusalem literally spits at you as you run away. "'Who do you think you've been dissing and disrespecting all this time? Who have you been sneering at with such arrogance? The Holy One of Israel! You sent your servants to mock the Master. You bragged, ‘With my army of chariots, I’ve conquered the highest mountains, explored the deepest parts of Lebanon, chopped down its best trees. I’ve reached its highest peak, explored its thickest forest. I dug wells and drank foreign water. I dried up all the famous rivers of Egypt with just the sole of my foot.’

"'But have you not heard? I planned all of this a long, long time ago. I'm the one who's making it happen now. I used you to turn strong cities into piles of rocks, leaving their people weak, helpless, and confused, like plants with no water.

"'I see your whole act—your arrogant strutting, your comings and goings, and yeah, the temper tantrums you throw against me. Because you've been raging against me, and your pride is off the charts, I'm gonna put a hook in your nose and a bit in your mouth. I'm gonna show you who's really in charge and send you right back where you came from.

"'And Hezekiah, here's the sign for you: This year, the harvest will be pretty weak, and next year won't be much better. But in the third year, everything will be back to normal. You'll plant and harvest just like before. The survivors of Judah will put down new roots and grow again. The people left in Jerusalem will get a fresh start. The zeal of the God of the Angel Armies will make it all happen.'

"And finally, here's God's final word on the king of Assyria: "'Don't worry. He won't even get into this city. He won't shoot a single arrow, raise a shield, or build a ramp against it. He's going back the way he came. He won't set one foot in this city. That's a promise from God. I'm protecting this city to save it, for my own honor and for the promise I made to David.'"

That very night, the Angel of God showed up and wrecked the Assyrian camp. He killed 185,000 Assyrian soldiers. When the sun came up, there was just an army of dead bodies. Sennacherib, the king of Assyria, got out of there as fast as he could and ran back home to Nineveh. One day, while he was praying in the temple of his god Nisroch, his own sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, murdered him. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon took over as king.

title: God Hits Rewind on a Sundial?! Hezekiah's Near-Death Experience
paragraphs: So, around that time, King Hezekiah got super sick—like, he was on the verge of death. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and was like, “God says you need to get your life in order and sort things out with your family. This is it. You’re going to die. You’re not getting better.”

Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and just started praying to God, like, “God, please, I’m begging you. Just remember how I’ve lived my life. I’ve been loyal to you, and my heart has been 100% yours. You’ve seen how I’ve lived and all the good things I’ve done.” And as he prayed, Hezekiah just broke down and cried these painful tears.

Then, God’s word came to Isaiah: “Go back and tell Hezekiah this message from me, the God of your ancestor David: ‘I heard your prayer. I saw your tears. And here’s what I’m going to do: I’m adding fifteen years to your life. Not only that, but I’m going to rescue you and this city from the king of Assyria. I’ve got this city covered.’

“‘And here’s the sign to prove that I, God, will do exactly what I promised. Watch this: You see the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz? I’m going to make it go backward ten steps.’” And that’s exactly what happened. The shadow from the setting sun actually went back ten notches on the dial.

This is a song that Hezekiah, the king of Judah, wrote after he got sick and then recovered: “I thought, ‘I’m in the prime of my life, and now I have to go? The rest of my years will be spent in death’s waiting room.’ No more experiencing God in the land of the living, no more seeing my neighbors or hanging out with friends. My body, this home I live in, is being torn down and packed away like a camper’s tent. My life felt like a finished carpet that I rolled up, and now God is cutting me off the loom, sweeping up the scraps at the end of the day. I cry out for help until morning. God feels like a lion, just beating me down, relentlessly trying to finish me off. I’m squawking like a scared chicken, moaning like a dove. My eyes are sore from looking up to heaven for help. ‘Master, I’m in trouble! You gotta get me out of this!’ But what’s the point? God himself said this would happen. He’s the one who did it. I’m so upset and troubled, I can’t even sleep.

“Oh Master, it’s in these tough situations that people truly live, and it’s in these same conditions that my spirit is still alive—I’m fully recovered, with a fresh start on life! It actually seems like it was good for me to go through all that trouble. Through it all, you held on to my life. You never let me slip and fall into nothingness. But my sins? You just let them go, threw them over your shoulder like they were nothing—good riddance! The dead can't thank you, and choirs in the morgue don’t sing praises. People buried six feet under can’t tell stories about your faithfulness. It’s the living—the men and women who are alive right now—who thank you, just like I’m doing. And parents tell their kids all about how faithful you are.
“God saves me and will keep saving me. So let the music start, we’ll sing and sing for the rest of our lives in God’s Sanctuary.”
Isaiah had told them, “Make a paste out of figs and put it on his boil, and he’ll recover.” And Hezekiah had asked, “What’s the sign that I’ll be able to go back to God’s Sanctuary again?”

title: Hezekiah's Epic Flex Backfires
paragraphs: A little while later, King Merodach-baladan, son of Baladan from Babylon, sent some messengers with a get-well gift and greetings for Hezekiah. He'd heard Hezekiah had been super sick but was all better now.

Hezekiah was totally stoked to see them and gave them a warm welcome. He took them on a full tour of his royal palace, basically flexing all his treasures: the silver, the gold, the fancy spices, the expensive oils, all his weapons—like, everything was out on display. There was literally nothing in his house or his entire kingdom that Hezekiah didn't show off to them.

Later, the prophet Isaiah came to see him. He asked Hezekiah, “So, what were those guys doing here? What did they have to say? And where'd they come from anyway?” Hezekiah said, “Oh, they came from a super far-off place, from Babylon.”
“And what did they see in your palace?” Isaiah asked. “Everything,” said Hezekiah. “I showed them the works, opened up all the doors. They were seriously impressed with all my stuff.”

Then Isaiah dropped a heavy message on Hezekiah from the God-of-the-Angel-Armies: "You need to listen up. I gotta warn you, the time is coming when everything in this palace, plus everything your ancestors saved up before you, is going to be hauled off to Babylon. God says there will be nothing left. Zero. And it's not just your stuff, but your sons too. Some of your own sons will be taken away, and they'll end up as eunuchs serving in the palace of the king of Babylon."

Hezekiah replied to Isaiah, “If God says so, that’s fine.” But lowkey, he was thinking to himself, “But for sure nothing bad will happen while I'm alive. I'll get to enjoy peace and quiet for the rest of my life.”

title: God's Ultimate Power Flex
paragraphs: "Comfort, oh comfort my people," says your God. "Talk to Jerusalem real gentle and sweet, but also make it super clear that her time-out is over. Her mess-ups? All taken care of—totally forgiven! She’s been through enough, like, way more than enough, and now it's all good."

A voice booms in the middle of nowhere! "Get ready for God's entrance! Make the road straight and smooth, a highway fit for our God. Fill in the low spots, flatten the hills, smooth out the bumps, and get rid of the rocks. Then God's awesome glory will shine for everyone to see. God said it, so it’s happening."

A voice says, "Shout!" I'm like, "Shout what?" "These people are basically like grass, and their love is as delicate as wildflowers. The grass dries up, the flowers fade, especially if God just breathes on them. Aren't people just a bunch of grass? Yeah, the grass withers and the flowers fade, but God's Word is forever."

Get up on a high mountain, Zion. You're the one with the good news. Use your outside voice, Jerusalem. You're the good news preacher. Shout it loud and clear. Don't be scared! Tell all the towns in Judah, "Look! It's your God!" Look at him! God, the Boss, is coming in with power, ready to make moves. He's about to pay back his haters and reward the ones who've been loyal. He'll take care of his crew like a shepherd, scooping up the little lambs in his arms, holding them close as he carries them, and leading the mama sheep to the best spots.

Who do you think scooped up the whole ocean in his hands, or measured the sky with his fingers? Who put all the dirt on earth in a single basket, and weighed every mountain and hill? Who could ever tell God what to do or give him pointers? What expert would he need to ask for advice? What school would he go to to learn about justice? What other god could have possibly taught him what he knows, or showed him how everything works? Honestly, all the nations are just a drop in a bucket, like a smudge on a window. Watch him sweep up islands like they're just dust on the floor! There aren't enough trees in Lebanon or enough animals in those huge forests to even be a decent offering for him. All the nations together are basically nothing to him—less than nothing, actually. A total minus.

So who's even on the same level as God? Who or what can you even compare him to? Some fake idol? That's ridiculous! It's just made in a workshop, covered in a thin layer of gold, and decorated with some silver chains. Or maybe someone picks out some fancy, non-rotting wood, and hires a dude to carve a fake god, making sure it won't fall over.

Have you been living under a rock? Have you not been listening? Haven't you heard these stories your whole life? Don't you get how things work? God is sitting high above this round earth. From his view, people look like tiny ants. He stretches out the sky like a giant canvas—yeah, like a tent to live in. He doesn't even pay attention to what princes and rulers say or do. The leaders of the world mean nothing to him. They're like seeds that have barely even sprouted. They just shrivel up when God blows on them. They're gone with the wind, like little specks of dust.

"So—who's like me? Who can even compare?" says the Holy One. Just look up at the night sky: Who do you think made all of this? Who brings out this army of stars every night, counts them, and calls every single one by name? He's so magnificent and powerful that he never loses a single one.

So why would you ever complain, Jacob, or whine, Israel, and say, "God has forgotten about me. He doesn't care what happens to me"? Have you been living under a rock or something? Haven't you been listening? God isn't some trend that comes and goes. God is forever. He created everything you can see or even imagine. He never gets tired, never needs a break. And he knows everything, inside and out. He gives energy to people who are tired and fresh strength to those who feel like giving up. Even young people get tired and quit; the best of the best stumble and fall. But anyone who waits for God gets fresh strength. They'll spread their wings and fly like eagles, they'll run and not get tired, they'll walk and won't fall behind.

title: God's Got Your Back, No Cap
paragraphs: “Alright, everyone, chill out and listen up. All you islands out there, take a seat. Get your energy back. Come on over, tell me what's up. Let's figure this out together.

“So, who kicked things off? Who got this hero from the east going? Who signed him up for this gig, gathered all the nations so he could totally own the kings? He's on a roll, turning nations into dust, just leaving scraps behind. He chases them down and doesn't even get a scratch, like his feet aren't even touching the ground.
“Who did all this? Who made it happen? Who's always the one to start things? That's me. God. I'm the first one here and the last one to leave.

“All the faraway islands see what's happening and they're freaking out. The whole world is shook. They're all huddled up, scared, running around asking, ‘What’s going to happen?’ The idol-makers are working overtime, cranking out new fake gods, telling each other, ‘Nice work!’ ‘Beautiful!’ and nailing them down so they don't fall over.

“But you, Israel, you're my crew. You're Jacob, my number one pick, the family of my good friend Abraham. I found you all over the world, called you from the darkest places, and told you, ‘You're my servant, you're on my team. I chose you. I’m not going to abandon you.’ So don't freak out. I'm with you. No need to be scared, because I'm your God. I'll make you strong. I'll help you out. I'll keep you steady and hold on tight.

“For real, everyone who's against you is gonna end up left out in the cold—total losers. The people who tried to bring you down will have nothing to show for it. When you try to find your old haters, you won't find them—not a single trace, not even a memory. You know why? Because I, your God, have a tight grip on you and I'm not letting go. I'm telling you, ‘Don't panic. I'm right here to help you.’

"Feeling like a worm, Jacob? Don't be scared. Feeling fragile like a bug, Israel? I got you. I, God, want to make sure you know. The God who saves you, the Holy One of Israel. I'm giving you a major glow-up, from a worm to a tractor, from a bug to solid iron. You'll be like a beast of a machine, smoothing out mountains and turning tough hills into soft dirt. You'll tear up the rough ground, exposing it to the sun, wind, and rain. And you’ll exult in God, glorying in the Holy of Israel!

“The poor and needy are desperate for water, their mouths are dry and there's none to be found. But I'm there for them, and I, the God of Israel, won't leave them hanging. I'll make rivers flow on dry hills and springs in the valleys. I’ll turn the desert into pools of water and the dry land into springs. I'll plant all kinds of trees in the wasteland—cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive. I'll put cypress, oak, and pine trees in the desert. Everyone will see it. It'll be super obvious, no-doubt-about-it proof that I, God, did this myself. It's all created and signed by the Holy One of Israel.

“‘Alright, make your case for your gods,’ says God. ‘Show me the receipts,’ says the King of Jacob. ‘Let your idols defend themselves, give me some arguments, some reasons. Lay out the facts so we can see for ourselves. Ask them, ‘If you're gods, what's the deal with the past—or if you can't do that, tell us the future. Can't do that either? How about you do something—anything! Good or bad—whatever. Can you hurt us or help us? Should we be scared of you?’ They don't say anything, because they're nothing—just fake gods, no-gods, gods that make you look like a fool.

“I, God, got someone started from the north, and he's here. I called him by name from the east. He's gonna stomp on rulers like they're mud, just like a potter squishes clay. Let me ask you, did anyone see this coming? Did anyone tell us this would happen so we could be like, ‘Yep, he was right!’? No one said a word, no one announced it, no one heard a peep from you. But I told Zion all about this from the start. I gave Jerusalem a messenger with good news. But over here, there's no one—no one knows what's going on. I ask, but no one can give me the scoop. It's all nothing. It's all smoke and mirrors—fake gods, empty gods, no-gods.”

title: God's GOATed Servant is Coming!
paragraphs: "Look at my special guy. I've got his back 100%. He's my chosen one, and I'm super proud of him. I've filled him with my Spirit, my very life. He’s gonna establish justice in the nations. He's not gonna be loud or showy about it. He won't ignore the broken or the hurting, and he won't diss the small and unimportant. He'll just keep on, steady and strong, making things right. He won't get tired and give up. He won't stop until he's done what he came to do - to fix things on earth. Even far-off islands are waiting to hear what he has to say.”

“This is a message from God, the one who made the whole universe, stretched out the sky, and made the earth and everything on it. The one who gives life to everyone. He says: 'I am God. I've called you to live a good and right life. I've got you, I'll keep you safe. I've put you here to connect my people to me, and to be a light for all the nations. To open blind eyes, to free people from their prisons, to bring them out of the darkness. I am God. That's my name. I don't share my glory with anyone, and I don't approve of fake gods. Listen up: the bad things I said would happen, have happened. Now I'm telling you about the new good things I'm going to do. Before it even starts, I'm giving you the inside scoop.'”

“Sing a new song to God, praise him all over the world! Let the ocean and all the fish in it cheer, and all the islands too. Let the desert and its people sing, and the nomads from Kedar join in. Let the people in Sela form a choir and sing from the mountaintops. Let God's glory be heard everywhere, from coast to coast. God is coming out like he's ready for a fight. You can tell he's about to do something big. He shouts, letting everyone know he's here. He takes control and his enemies are defeated: 'I've been quiet for too long. I've held back, kept my mouth shut. But now I'm letting it all out, like a woman giving birth - I'm going to destroy the hills, kill the flowers, dry up the rivers, and turn lakes into mud. But for those who are lost and can't see the way, I'll hold their hand. I'll be their personal guide, leading them through places they don't know. I'll be right there to show them the right paths, and make sure they don't mess up. I'll do all this for them - I'll stick with them, I won't leave them for a second.'”
"But for those who invested in fake gods, it's the end—they're totally broke."

“Hello? Are you deaf? Open your eyes! Are you blind? You're my servant, but you're not even looking! You're my messenger, but you're not listening! The very people I was counting on, God's servants, are acting like they're blind on purpose! You've seen a lot, but you haven't really looked at anything. You've heard everything, but you haven't really listened to anything. God wanted to show you so much, because he's so good. But now his people are beaten down and scared, hiding in their rooms. They're victims, feeling hurt and ignored. Is anyone out there listening? Is anyone paying attention to what's coming? Who do you think let Jacob get beat up by thugs, and let robbers attack Israel? Wasn't it God himself, the God we sinned against? We didn't do what he said, we didn't listen to him. Isn't that why God is so angry, and why he's punishing them? Their whole world fell apart but they still didn't get it; their life is a mess but they don't care.”

title: God's Got Your Back, No Cap
paragraphs: But listen up, this is God talking. The God who literally created you, Jacob, the one who made you, Israel. He's saying: 'Don't even trip, I got you. I've called you by your name. You're my person. When you feel like you're drowning, I'll be right there with you. When you're going through some rough stuff, you won't get taken out. When you're stuck between a rock and a hard place, it's not game over. Why? Because I'm God, *your* God, the Holy One of Israel, your personal Savior. I paid a crazy price for you—like, all of Egypt, plus the super-rich Cush and Seba. That's how much you're worth to me. That’s how much I love you. I'd literally trade the whole world to get you back, the entire universe just for you.'

'So for real, don't be scared. I'm with you. I'm gonna gather all your scattered people, bring them back from all over the place, east and west. I'll tell the north and south, 'Send them back. Bring my sons from far away, my daughters from the ends of the earth. I want every single one of them back, everyone who carries my name, every single person I created for my own glory, the ones I personally made.'

'Now, bring out the blind and deaf people—the ones who are blind but have perfectly good eyes, and the ones who are deaf but have perfectly good ears. Then get all the other nations together. Let's see what they have to say. How do they explain everything that's happened? Let them bring their best witnesses and make their case; let them try to prove they're right. 'But you guys are my witnesses.' This is God's decree. 'You're the servant I chose so that you'll get to know and trust me, and understand that I'm the real deal. Before me, there was no such thing as a god, and there won't be one after me. I, yeah, I'm God. I'm the only Savior, period. I'm the one who spoke, who saved, who told you what was up way before these new fake gods showed up. And you know it, you're my proof.' God's decree. 'Yep, I am God. I've always been God and I always will be. No one can snatch anything out of my hand. I do things; who can undo them?'

God, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, says: 'Just for you, I'm about to march on Babylon. I'm gonna flip the script on the Babylonians. Instead of partying, they'll be crying. I am God, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.'

This is what God says, the same God who builds a highway through the ocean and carves a path through massive waves, the God who calls out armies with their horses and chariots—they lie down and can't get back up; they're snuffed out like candles: 'Forget what happened in the past; don't get stuck on old history. Pay attention, be present. I'm about to do something totally new. It's happening right now! Can't you see it? There it is! I'm making a road in the middle of the desert, and rivers in the dry badlands. Even the wild animals will thank me—the coyotes and buzzards—because I gave them water in the desert, rivers in the sun-scorched land, drinking water for the people I chose, the people I made just for me, a people custom-designed to sing my praises.'

'But you, Jacob, you didn't pay any attention to me. You got tired of me so fast, Israel. You didn't even bring me sheep for worship. You couldn't be bothered with sacrifices. It's not like I was asking for a lot. I didn't expect crazy expensive gifts. But you didn't even do the bare minimum—you were so stingy with me. But when it came to your sins, you weren't stingy at all. You were super generous with those—and I'm worn out by it.'
'But me, yeah me, I'm the one who wipes your sins clean—that's just what I do. I don't keep a running list of all your mess-ups.'

'So, go ahead, make your case against me. Let's argue it out. Give me your best shot. Prove you're in the right. Your very first ancestor was the one who started sinning, and every leader since then has just kept it going. That's why I had to disqualify your Temple leaders, disown Jacob, and disgrace Israel.'

title: God vs. Idols: The Ultimate ROAST
paragraphs: “But listen up, my servant Jacob—yeah, you, Israel, the one I hand-picked. The God who made you, who formed you from the jump, wants to help you out. So don’t be scared, my guy Jacob, Jeshurun, my chosen one. I’m about to pour water on thirsty ground and make streams flow through the dry dirt. I’ll pour my Spirit on your kids and my blessing on their kids. They’ll pop up like grass on the prairie, like willow trees by the water. One person will say, ‘I’m with God,’ and another will be like, ‘Team Jacob.’ Someone else will write ‘God’s Property’ on their hand and be proud to be called Israel.”

God, the King of Israel, your Redeemer, the Lord of the Angel Armies, says this: “I’m the first, I’m the last, and everything in between. I’m the only God, for real. Who can even compare to me? Go ahead, speak up. See if you can measure up. Who else has been calling the shots from the beginning? So what’s next? Anyone wanna take a guess? Don’t be afraid, don’t even trip. Haven’t I always told you what’s up? You’re my witnesses. Have you ever seen another God, a real one, besides me? There’s no Rock like me, period.”

All those people making fake gods are a joke, and the stuff they work so hard on is worthless. Their little puppet-gods can’t see and don’t know anything—they’re a total fail. Who would even make gods that can’t do anything, that can’t even be gods? Just watch, all the idol worshipers are gonna be so embarrassed. Watch the idol makers get all humiliated when their creations do nothing. Let’s get them all out here and make them face the facts.
The blacksmith makes his fake god, hammering it out in the fire on his anvil—so much work! He’s getting tired, hungry, and thirsty.

The woodworker draws up a plan for his fake god, traces it on some wood. He carves it with his tools, making it look like a person—a beautiful human—and puts it in a shrine. First, he cuts down a cedar, or maybe a pine or an oak, and lets it get strong in the forest, drinking up the rain. Then he uses it for two things: part of it for firewood to stay warm and bake bread, and the other part to make a god he worships. He carves it into a god-shape and prays to it. With half, he makes a fire to warm up and cook his dinner. He eats until he’s full and then kicks back, happy with a full stomach and warm feet, thinking, “Ah, this is the life.” And he still has the other half left for a god, a custom-made fake god to worship whenever he feels like it. Whenever he needs something, he prays to it, “Save me. You’re my god.”

Pretty stupid, right? Don’t they have eyes in their heads? Are their brains even working? Does it not hit them to say, “I used half of this tree for firewood, baked bread, and cooked meat. And now I used the rest to make this gross fake god. I’m literally praying to a piece of wood!”

This lover of emptiness is so out of touch with reality, so far gone, that he can’t even see what he’s doing. He can’t even look at the fake god, the piece of wood in his hand, and say, “This is wild.”

“Remember this, Jacob. Get this, Israel: you’re my servant. I made you, I shaped you. You’re my servant. Israel, I’ll never forget you. I’ve wiped your slate clean of all your mistakes. Your sins are gone. Come back to me, come back. I’ve saved you.”
Sing, you heavens! God did that. Shout, deep earth! And you mountains, sing! A whole forest choir of oaks, pines, and cedars! God has redeemed Jacob. God’s glory is on full display in Israel.
God, your Redeemer, who shaped you in your mother’s womb, says: “I am God. I made everything. I spread out the skies and laid out the earth all by myself.”

He makes magicians look like fools and turns fortunetellers into a joke. He makes the so-called experts look dumb and their “knowledge” look silly. But he backs up the words of his servant and makes his messengers’ advice come true. He says to Jerusalem, “You’ll be lived in again,” and to the cities of Judah, “You’ll be rebuilt,” and to the ruins, “I’m raising you up.” He says to the ocean, “Dry up. I’m drying up your rivers.” He says to Cyrus, “My shepherd—you’ll do everything I want.” He says to Jerusalem, “Be built,” and to the Temple, “Be established.”

title: God's Ultimate Flex: He Does What He Wants
paragraphs: This is God's message for his chosen one, Cyrus. God took him by the hand and gave him the job of schooling nations and making their kings tremble. He gave him a total green light, no limits. "I'll go ahead of you, smoothing out the road. I'll smash through bronze city gates, break open padlocks, and kick down any barred doors. I'll lead you to secret stashes of treasure and hidden valuables. This is all to prove that it's really me, God, the God of Israel, who's calling you by your name. It’s all for Jacob, my servant, my chosen people Israel, that I've picked you out, called you by name, and given you this great work. And you don't even know who I am! I'm God, the one and only. There are no other real gods besides me. I'm the one who geared you up for this, even though you don't know me, so that everyone, from sunrise to sunset, will know I have no competition. I am God, the only one. I create light and I make darkness; I bring peace and I cause chaos. I, God, do all of this.

"Open up, skies, and let it rain. Clouds, pour down my goodness! Earth, open up and let salvation bloom; let righteousness sprout. I, God, am making all this happen. But it's game over for you who argue with your own Maker—you're like a clay pot fighting the potter! Does the clay ever talk back to the potter and say, 'Yo, what are you doing? Your hands are clumsy!' Would a kid ever say to his dad, 'Who said you get to decide how I was made?' Or to his mom, 'Why did you give birth to me like this?'"

This is what God, the Holy One of Israel, Israel's Maker, says: "Are you seriously questioning what I'm creating? Are you trying to tell me what I can and can't do? I made the earth, and I created people to live on it. I built the skies with my own hands and I command all the stars. And now, I've set Cyrus in motion. I've rolled out the red carpet for him. He's going to rebuild my city and bring my exiled people home. I didn't pay him to do this. I commanded him. I, the God-of-Angel-Armies, said so."

God says: "The workers from Egypt, the merchants from Ethiopia, and those tall Sabeans will all come over to you—they'll be all yours. They’ll follow you in chains, bowing down and praying to you, saying, 'Wow, God is really with you! There's no other God—not a single one.'"

For real, you're a God who works behind the scenes, God of Israel, the Savior. All those other guys who make fake gods will be totally humiliated and embarrassed to even show their faces. They'll be jobless and confused, not knowing what to do with themselves. But the people of Israel are saved by you, God, with a salvation that lasts forever. They'll never be ashamed or left hanging, ever.

God, the one who created the heavens—He is the God, for real. The one who made the earth—He set it on its foundations and built it from the ground up. He didn't go through all that effort just to leave it empty. He made it to be lived in. This God says: "I am God, the one and only. I don't whisper to myself or mumble in secret. I never told Jacob's crew, 'Go look for me in an empty, dark void.' I am God. I do things out in the open, saying what's right and making things right. So gather 'round, come on in, all you who've been kicked out and cast aside. They don't get it, do they? The ones carrying around their useless wooden idols, praying for help to a dead piece of wood. So tell me what you think. Look at the facts. Put your heads together and state your case. Who told you what was happening way back when? Who made it all make sense for you? Wasn't it me? God? It had to be me. I'm the only God there is—the only God who does what's right and knows how to save. So turn to me and be saved!—everyone, no matter who or where you are. I am God, the only God there is, period. I swear on my own name: Every word I say is true and does what it's supposed to do. I never take back my words. Everyone will eventually kneel before me. Everyone will end up saying about me, 'Yes! Real salvation and strength are in God!'"

Everyone who got mad and raged against him will be brought before him, totally embarrassed by their lack of faith. And everyone connected to Israel will live a strong, praise-filled, good life in God!

title: God vs. Idols: Who's REALLY Carrying You?
paragraphs: The so-called god Bel totally face-plants, and Nebo just slumps over. These no-god hunks of wood get loaded onto mules and have to be hauled off, which is totally exhausting for the poor animals. They're just dead weight, these burdens who can't even carry themselves, getting dragged off to who-knows-where.

"Listen to me, family of Jacob, everyone that's left of the family of Israel. I've been carrying you on my back from the day you were born, and I'll keep on carrying you when you're old. I'll be there, bearing you when you're old and gray. I've done it and will keep on doing it, carrying you on my back, saving you.

"So who are you going to compare me to, the Incomparable? Can you even picture me without totally downgrading me? People with a lot of money hire craftsmen to make them gods. The artisan delivers the god, and they kneel and worship it! They carry it around in holy parades, then take it home and put it on a shelf. And there it sits, day in and day out, a dependable god, always right where you put it. Say anything you want to it, it never talks back. Of course, it never does anything either!

"Think about this. Seriously, wrap your minds around it. This is a big deal, you rebels. Take it to heart. Remember your history, your long and rich history. I am God, the only God you've had or ever will have—incomparable, irreplaceable. From the very beginning, I was telling you what the ending will be. All along, I've been letting you in on what is going to happen, assuring you, 'I'm in this for the long haul, I'll do exactly what I set out to do,' calling that eagle, Cyrus, out of the east, from a far country—the man I chose to help me. I've said it, and I'll most certainly do it. I've planned it, so it's as good as done.

"Now listen to me: You're a hardheaded bunch and tough to help. But I'm ready to help you right now. Deliverance is not some long-range plan. Salvation isn't on hold. I'm putting salvation to work in Zion now, and my glory in Israel."

title: Babylon's Epic Fail
paragraphs: Alright Babylon, get off your high horse. Time to sit in the dirt. No more throne for you—sit on the ground, Chaldeans. No one's gonna be calling you 'charming' or 'alluring' anymore. Get used to it. Get a real job for once: clean gutters, scrub toilets. Pawn your fancy clothes, put on some work pants—the party's over. You're gonna be totally exposed, and people are gonna be ruthless with their comments. It's payback time, and I'm not letting anyone off the hook.

Our Redeemer, the one they call the God-of-the-Angel-Armies, the Holy One of Israel, says: “Shut up and get out of the way, daughter of Chaldeans. You’re not gonna be called ‘First Lady of the Kingdoms’ anymore.” I was so done with my people, legit disgusted with them. I handed them over to you, but you showed zero compassion. You made the elderly do cruel, hard labor. You were all like, ‘I’m the First Lady. I’ll always be the pampered darling.’ You didn't take anything seriously, never really thought about the consequences. Well, start thinking, playgirl. You act like you're the center of the universe, smugly thinking, ‘I’m Number One. There’s no one else but me. I’ll never be a widow, I’ll never lose my kids.’ But BAM, those two things are gonna hit you at the same time, out of nowhere, on the same day: your husband and kids, gone. A total loss, no matter how many magic tricks and charms you have. You were so confident in your messed-up life, thinking, ‘No one sees me.’ You thought you were so smart, had it all figured out. What a joke! So smug, telling yourself, ‘I’m Number One. There’s nobody but me.’ But ruin is coming, and you can't charm it away. Disaster's gonna strike, and you can't use a spell to get rid of it. It'll be a total catastrophe, and you'll be completely lost, totally bewildered. But hey, don't give up. You've got a whole bunch of enchantments, right? There must be one you haven't tried. You've been doing this for a long time. Surely something will work. I know you're exhausted from trying all your little remedies, but don't give up. Call in your astrologers and stargazers. They're good at this stuff. Surely they can cook something up!

Yeah, right. You'd be grasping at straws that are already on fire. A fire that's raging right now. Your so-called 'experts' are in it and they're not getting out. This isn't some cozy campfire for cooking stew or warming up on a winter night! That's what's gonna happen to your sorcerer friends, your magician buddies you've been scheming with your whole life. They're stumbling around, all confused, bumping into each other. And not a single one of them is gonna bother to help you.

title: God's Epic Plan vs. Our Stubborn Ways
paragraphs: Alright, listen up, fam of Jacob, everyone who's called Israel. You're from the line of Judah, and you use God's name when you make promises and pray to the God of Israel. But are you for real? Do you actually live like it? You claim to be from the Holy City and act like you rely on the God of Israel, the one called God-of-the-Angel-Armies. For a while now, I've been telling you how I work: I'd tell you what I was going to do, then I'd do it, and it was a done deal. That's it. I know you're all a bunch of stubborn hardheads. So I gave you a heads-up and told you what was going to happen before it even went down. That way, you can't say, 'My idol did this,' or 'My favorite statue ordered this.' You've seen and heard all the evidence. Shouldn't you be talking about it? And that was just the beginning. I have so much more to tell you, things you never even knew about. This is something totally new, not just a remix of the old stuff. It's brand-new, something you couldn't have guessed or dreamed of. When you hear it, you won't be able to say, 'Oh, I knew that was coming.' You've never been good at listening to me. You've got a history of ignoring me, a bad habit of being disloyal—rebels from day one. But because I'm good and because of who I am, I'm holding back my anger. I'm not giving up on you. See what I've done? I've refined you, but it took some fire. I've tested you in the furnace of suffering. I do what I do for my own sake, because of who I am. I have a reputation to protect. I'm not taking a backseat to any gods or people.

“Listen, Jacob. Listen, Israel—I'm the one who named you! I'm the One. I started everything, and I'll be the one to finish it. The earth is my handmade creation. And the skies—I made them too, from one end to the other. When I give the word, they stand at attention.

“Everyone, get together and listen up: Which of the gods has ever told you this stuff? I, God, love this guy Cyrus, and I'm using him to do what I want to Babylon. I'm the one who has spoken. I've called him. I've brought him here. He's going to succeed. Come closer, listen carefully: I've never kept things secret from you. I've always been here with you.”

And now, the Master, God, sends me and his Spirit with this message from God your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am God, your God, who teaches you how to live right and well. I show you what to do and where to go. If you had just listened to what I told you, your life would have been like a flowing river, with blessings rolling in like ocean waves. You would have had kids and grandkids as numerous as the sand, so many you couldn't count. You would never have been in danger of being cut off from me.”
Get out of Babylon! Run from the Babylonians! Shout the news. Tell everyone. Let the whole world know. Tell them, “God has saved his servant Jacob!”
They weren't thirsty when he led them through the deserts. He made water pour out of a rock for them; he split the rock, and water gushed out.
“But for the wicked,” says God, “there is no peace.”

title: God's Ultimate Comeback Plan
paragraphs: Listen up, all you people from far away! God basically hired me before I was even born. The second I came into the world, He knew my name. He gave me a voice that’s sharp and gets right to the point. He’s always had my back, keeping me safe. He treated me like his secret weapon, his best arrow, kept hidden until the right time. He told me, “You’re my special servant, Israel, and I’m going to show my greatness through you.”
But honestly, I was feeling like, “I’ve worked for nothing. I have zero to show for all this hard work.” Still, I decided to let God have the final say. I’ll let Him be the judge of my life’s work.

And now, God is speaking—the same God who shaped me from birth to be his servant, to bring his people, Jacob and Israel, back to him. It’s a huge honor, for real, and God is my strength. He says, “Just bringing back the tribes of Jacob and the lost people of Israel? That’s not a big enough job for you. I’m making you a light for all the nations, so my salvation can go global!”

This is what God, the Redeemer and the Holy One of Israel, says to the one who is looked down on, hated by nations, and a slave to rulers: “Kings will see you and stand up in respect. Princes will see you and bow down. It’s all because of God, who is faithful and has chosen you.”

God also says: “When the time is right, I’ll answer you. On the day of victory, I’ll be there to help you. I made you, and I’m using you to bring my people back to me, to restore the land, and to give back the ruined properties to their families. I’m telling the prisoners, ‘You’re free! Come on out!’ and to those hiding in darkness, ‘It’s safe now, you can come out.’ They’ll find food everywhere they go, like a feast on every hill. No one will be hungry or thirsty. They’ll be protected from the heat and wind, because the God of compassion is guiding them to the best springs of water. I’ll turn all my mountains into roads, making a superhighway for them. Look! People are coming from all over—from the north, from the west, and even from as far as Egypt!”
Heavens, let’s get loud! Earth, wake up! Mountains, start cheering! God has comforted his people. He has been so gentle and kind to his people who were beaten down and hurting.
But the people of Zion said, “I don’t get it. God has totally left me. My Lord has forgotten I even exist.”

“Can a mother forget her own baby? Can she walk away from the child she gave birth to? Even if a mother could forget, I will never, ever forget you. Look, I’ve basically tattooed your name on my hands. I’m always watching over the walls you’re rebuilding. Your builders are working faster than your destroyers ever did. The demolition crews are gone for good. Look up, look around you! See all your people gathering and coming back to you? As surely as I am the living God,” says the Lord, “you will wear them like jewelry. You’ll be decked out with them like a bride on her wedding day.”

“And what about your ruined, devastated land? It’s about to be filled with so many people you won’t know what to do! Your enemies will be a distant memory. The children who were born while you were in exile will say, ‘It’s getting way too crowded here. I need more space!’ And you’ll think to yourself, ‘Where did all these kids come from? I lost everything, I was exiled and alone. Who raised all these children? How did they even get here?’”

The Master, God, says: “Watch! I’ll signal to the nations, I’ll raise my flag for all the people to see. And they will bring your sons and daughters back to you, carrying them in their arms and on their shoulders. Kings will be like your babysitters, and princesses will be your nannies. They’ll even do your chores—scrub your floors and do your laundry. Then you will know that I am God. No one who puts their hope in me will ever be disappointed.”

Can you take back treasure from a giant? Can you rescue prisoners from a tyrant? But God says, “Even if a giant has the treasure and a tyrant holds my people captive, I am on your side. I will defend you and rescue your children. And your enemies will go crazy and turn on each other, destroying themselves in a mad frenzy. Then everyone on earth will know that I, God, have saved you—I, the Mighty One of Jacob.”

title: God's Got Your Back, So Who's Gonna Mess With You?
paragraphs: God's like, 'Where are the divorce papers? Show me the evidence. You think I just divorced your mom, your nation, for no reason? You think I sold you off like some old video game? Nah. The truth is, you guys messed up. Your sins are what got you into this mess, your wrongs are why you got shipped out. I showed up, ready to help, but nobody was home. I called, and all I got was voicemail. You think I'm washed up? That I can't do anything? I'm the same God who can turn the sea into a desert with a single word, leaving fish to rot in the sun. I can literally turn off the lights in the sky.'

The big boss, God, has trained me to speak well, so I know how to lift people up when they're feeling down. He wakes me up every single morning, opens my ears to listen like a student ready for class. And when God speaks, I don't just roll over and go back to sleep. I get up and do what He says. I stood my ground when they beat me, I didn't flinch when they ripped out my beard. I took their insults, let them spit in my face. And through it all, God was right there with me, so I wasn't embarrassed. That's why I can be so tough, like a rock. I know I won't regret this. My number one supporter is right here. Let's see who wants to start something! Who dares to sue me? Bring it on! Look, God is on my side. Who can say I'm guilty? All my haters are like a pile of old, worn-out clothes, just waiting to be eaten by moths.

So, who out there actually respects God and listens to His servant? If you're lost and don't know where you're going, stumbling in the dark, here's a tip: Trust God. Lean on Him. But if you're just out to cause trouble, to play with fire, go for it. See how that works out for you. Start your drama, fan the flames, but don't think I'm just going to sit back and watch. I'll make you face the consequences of your own actions.

title: God's Ultimate Comeback & Promise
paragraphs: "Listen, yes listen. If you’re serious about living a good life and you’re actually trying to connect with God, think about where you came from. Think about the rock you were cut from, the quarry you were dug out of. Yeah, think about your ancestor Abraham, and Sarah who gave birth to you. It’s wild, right? I called him when he was just one dude, but I blessed him and he became a whole nation. In the same way, I, God, am gonna comfort Zion and all its broken-down places. I’m gonna turn its dead ground into a new Eden, its empty landscape into my own garden. It’ll be a place full of hype and laughter, with people singing thank-you songs and jamming out.

“Pay attention, my people. Listen to me, all you nations. My truth is about to drop, and my decisions will be like a light for the whole world. My rescue is coming in hot, my salvation is right on time. I’m gonna bring justice for everyone. Even far-off islands are gonna look to me and put their hope in my power to save them. Look up at the sky, then look down at the earth. The sky’s gonna disappear like smoke, the earth is gonna get worn out like old jeans, and everyone on it will die like flies. But my salvation? That’s forever. My way of making things right will never get old.

“So listen up, you who get the difference between right and wrong, you who keep my teachings in your heart: Don’t even sweat the haters, and when people mock you, don’t let it get to you. Those insults are weak, like clothes eaten by moths, coming from minds that are basically termite-infested. But my plan to make things right will last forever, and my salvation goes on and on and on.”

Come on, God, wake up! Flex those muscles! Show up like you did back in the day, ages ago. Weren’t you the one who totally wrecked Rahab and took down that ancient chaos-dragon? And didn’t you dry up the sea, the super deep waters, and then build a road on the ocean floor for your rescued people to walk across? That’s how your ransomed people are gonna come back. They’ll return to Zion cheering, with endless joy on their faces, so hyped and ecstatic they can’t even stand it—and you won’t hear any moaning or groaning.

“It’s me. I’m the one comforting you. So why are you so scared? Of some person who’s just gonna die anyway? Some poor human who’s gonna turn to dust? You totally forgot about me, your God, the one who made you, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. And now you’re here, shaking like a leaf because some bully is throwing a fit and thinks he can destroy the world. But what’s gonna happen to his tantrums? Nothing. The prisoners will be set free before you know it. They’re not gonna die. They won’t even go hungry. Because I am God, your God, the one who stirs up the sea and makes the waves crash. My name is the Lord of Angel Armies. I give you the words to say, and I personally protect you, even while I’m creating new heavens, setting the earth on a firm foundation, and telling Zion, ‘You’re my people!’"

So wake up! Get the sleep out of your eyes! Get on your feet, Jerusalem! You drank the cup God gave you, that strong drink of his anger. You chugged the whole thing down to the last drop, and now you’re staggering around, totally wasted. And there was no one to help you get home. None of your so-called friends or your own kids would even take your hand and help you to bed. You got hit with a double whammy of trouble—does anyone even care? Violence and ruin, starvation and death—is anyone gonna comfort you? Your kids have all passed out, lying in the streets like stunned animals, knocked out by the strong drink of God’s anger, the fury of your God.

So listen up, you who are suffering with a massive headache, you who have a hangover that isn’t even from alcohol. Your Master, your God, has something to say. Your God is defending his people: “Look, I’ve taken back that cup of drink that made you stumble. You’re done drinking from that jug of my anger. I’ve handed it over to your abusers, the ones who told you, ‘Get on the ground so we can walk all over you!’ And you had to do it. You lay flat on the ground, and you became the dirt they walked on.”
